तमस्तमःकार्यमनर्थजालं न दृश्यते सत्युदिते दिनेशे ।
तथाद्वयानन्दरसानुभूतौ न वास्ति बन्धो न च दुःखगन्धः ॥ ३१९ ॥
319.transliteration:
tamastamaḥkāryamanarthajālaṃ na dṛśyate satyudite dineśe |
tathādvayānandarasānubhūtau na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ || 319 ||
319.translation: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

320.shloka:
दृश्यं प्रतीतं प्रविलापयन्सन् सन्मात्रमानन्दघनं विभावयन् ।
समाहितः सन्बहिरन्तरं वा कालं नयेथाः सति कर्मबन्धे ॥ ३२0 ॥
320.transliteration:
dṛśyaṃ pratītaṃ pravilāpayansan sanmātramānandaghanaṃ vibhāvayan |
samāhitaḥ sanbahirantaraṃ vā kālaṃ nayethāḥ sati karmabandhe || 320 ||
320.translation: Causing the external and internal universe, which are now perceived, to vanish, and meditating on the Reality, the Bliss Embodied, one should pass one’s time watchfully, if there be any residue of Prārabdha work left.

321.shloka:
प्रमादो ब्रह्मनिष्ठायां न कर्तव्यः कदाचन ।
प्रमादो मृत्युरित्याह भगवान्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥ ३२१ ॥
321.transliteration:
pramādo brahmaniṣṭhāyāṃ na kartavyaḥ kadācana |
pramādo mṛtyurityāha bhagavānbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 321 ||
321.translation: One should never be careless in one’s steadfastness to Brahman. Bhagavan Sanatkumāra, who is Brahma’s son, has called inadvertence to be death itself.

322.shloka:
न प्रमादादनर्थोऽन्यो ज्ञानिनः स्वस्वरूपतः ।
ततो मोहस्ततोऽहंधीस्ततो बन्धस्ततो व्यथा ॥ ३२२ ॥
322.transliteration:
na pramādādanartho'nyo jñāninaḥ svasvarūpataḥ |
tato mohastato'haṃdhīstato bandhastato vyathā || 322 ||
322.translation: There is no greater danger for the Jñānin than carelessness about his own real nature. From this comes delusion, thence egoism, this is followed by bondage, and then comes misery.

323.shloka:
विषयाभिमुखं दृष्ट्वा विद्वांसमपि विस्मृतिः ।
विक्षेपयति धीदोषैर्योषा जारमिव प्रियम् ॥ ३२३ ॥
323.transliteration:
viṣayābhimukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidvāṃsamapi vismṛtiḥ |
vikṣepayati dhīdoṣairyoṣā jāramiva priyam || 323 ||
323.translation: Finding even a wise man hankering after the sense-objects, oblivion torments him through the evil propensities of the Buddhi, as a woman does her doting paramour.

324.shloka:
यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति ।
आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥ ३२४ ॥
324.transliteration:
yathāpakṛṣṭaṃ śaivālaṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ na tiṣṭhati |
āvṛṇoti tathā māyā prājñaṃ vāpi parāṅmukham || 324 ||
324.translation: As moss, even if removed, does not stay away for a moment, but covers the water again, so Māyā or Nescience also covers even a wise man, if he is averse to meditation on the Self.

325.shloka:
लक्ष्यच्युतं चेद्यदि चित्तमीषद् बहिर्मुखं सन्निपतेत्ततस्ततः ।
प्रमादतः प्रच्युतकेलिकन्दुकः सोपानपङ्क्तौ पतितो यथा तथा ॥ ३२५ ॥
325.transliteration:
lakṣyacyutaṃ cedyadi cittamīṣad bahirmukhaṃ sannipatettatastataḥ |
pramādataḥ pracyutakelikandukaḥ sopānapaṅktau patito yathā tathā || 325 ||
325.translation: If the mind ever so slightly strays from the Ideal and becomes outgoing, then it goes down and down, just as a play-ball inadvertently dropped on the staircase bounds down from one step to another.

326.shloka:
विषयेष्वाविशच्चेतः संकल्पयति तद्गुणान् ।
सम्यक्संकल्पनात्कामः कामात्पुंसः प्रवर्तनम् ॥ ३२६ ॥
326.transliteration:
viṣayeṣvāviśaccetaḥ saṃkalpayati tadguṇān |
samyaksaṃkalpanātkāmaḥ kāmātpuṃsaḥ pravartanam || 326 ||
326.translation: The mind that is attached to the sense-objects reflects on their qualities; from mature reflection arises desire, and after desiring a man sets about having that thing.

327.shloka:
अतः प्रमादान्न परोऽस्ति मृत्युः विवेकिनो ब्रह्मविदः समाधौ ।
समाहितः सिद्धिमुपैति सम्यक् समाहितात्मा भव सावधानः ॥ ३२७ ॥
327.transliteration:
ataḥ pramādānna paro'sti mṛtyuḥ vivekino brahmavidaḥ samādhau |
samāhitaḥ siddhimupaiti samyak samāhitātmā bhava sāvadhānaḥ || 327 ||
327.translation: Hence to the discriminating knower of Brahman there is no worse death than inadvertence with regard to concentration. But the man who is concentrated attains complete success. (Therefore) carefully concentrate thy mind (on Brahman).

328.shloka:
ततः स्वरूपविभ्रंशो विभ्रष्टस्तु पतत्यधः ।
पतितस्य विना नाशं पुनर्नारोह ईक्ष्यते ॥ ३२८ ॥
328.transliteration:
tataḥ svarūpavibhraṃśo vibhraṣṭastu patatyadhaḥ |
patitasya vinā nāśaṃ punarnāroha īkṣyate || 328 ||
328.translation: Through inadvertence a man deviates from his real nature, and the man who has thus deviated falls. The fallen man comes to ruin, and is scarcely seen to rise again.

329.shloka:
संकल्पं वर्जयेत्तस्मात्सर्वानर्थस्य कारणम् ।
जीवतो यस्य कैवल्यं विदेहे स च केवलः यत्किंचित्पश्यतो भेदं भयं ब्रूते यजुःश्रुतिः ॥ ३२९ ॥
329.transliteration:
saṃkalpaṃ varjayettasmātsarvānarthasya kāraṇam |
jīvato yasya kaivalyaṃ videhe sa ca kevalaḥ yatkiṃcitpaśyato bhedaṃ bhayaṃ brūte yajuḥśrutiḥ || 329 ||
329.translation: Therefore one should give up reflecting on the sense-objects, which is the root of all mischief. He who is completely aloof even while living, is alone aloof after the dissolution of the body. The Yajur-Veda declares that there is fear for one who sees the least bit of distinction.

330.shloka:
यदा कदा वापि विपश्चिदेष ब्रह्मण्यनन्तेऽप्यणुमात्रभेदम् ।
पश्यत्यथामुष्य भयं तदैव यद्वीक्षितं भिन्नतया प्रमादात् ॥ ३३0 ॥
330.transliteration:
yadā kadā vāpi vipaścideṣa brahmaṇyanante'pyaṇumātrabhedam |
paśyatyathāmuṣya bhayaṃ tadaiva yadvīkṣitaṃ bhinnatayā pramādāt || 330 ||
330.translation: Whenever the wise man sees the least difference in the infinite Brahman, at once that which he sees as different through mistake, becomes a source of terror to him.

331.shloka:
श्रुतिस्मृतिन्यायशतैर्निषिद्धे दृश्येऽत्र यः स्वात्ममतिं करोति ।
उपैति दुःखोपरि दुःखजातं निषिद्धकर्ता स मलिम्लुचो यथा ॥ ३३१ ॥
331.transliteration:
śrutismṛtinyāyaśatairniṣiddhe dṛśye'tra yaḥ svātmamatiṃ karoti |
upaiti duḥkhopari duḥkhajātaṃ niṣiddhakartā sa malimluco yathā || 331 ||
331.translation: He who identifies himself with the objective universe which has been denied by hundreds of Shrutis, Smritis and reasonings, experiences misery after misery, like a thief, for he does something forbidden.

332.shloka:
सत्याभिसंधानरतो विमुक्तो महत्त्वमात्मीयमुपैति नित्यम् ।
मिथ्याभिसन्धानरतस्तु नश्येद् दृष्टं तदेतद्यदचौरचौरयोः ॥ ३३२ ॥
332.transliteration:
satyābhisaṃdhānarato vimukto mahattvamātmīyamupaiti nityam |
mithyābhisandhānaratastu naśyed dṛṣṭaṃ tadetadyadacauracaurayoḥ || 332 ||
332.translation: He who has devoted himself to meditation on the Reality (Brahman) and is free from Nescience, attains to the eternal glory of the Ātman. But he who dwells on the unreal (the universe) is destroyed. That this is so is evidenced in the case of one who is not a thief and one who is a thief.

333.shloka:
यतिरसदनुसन्धिं बन्धहेतुं विहाय स्वयमायामहमस्मीत्यात्मदृष्ट्यैव तिष्ठेत् ।
सुखयति ननु निष्ठा ब्रह्मणि स्वानुभूत्या हरति परमविद्याकार्यदुःखं प्रतीतम् ॥ ३३३ ॥
333.transliteration:
yatirasadanusandhiṃ bandhahetuṃ vihāya svayaMāyāmahamasmītyātmadṛṣṭyaiva tiṣṭhet |
sukhayati nanu niṣṭhā brahmaṇi svānubhūtyā harati paramavidyākāryaduḥkhaṃ pratītam || 333 ||
333.translation: The Sannyasin should give up dwelling on the unreal, which causes bondage, and should always fix his thoughts on the Ātman as 'I myself am This'. For the steadfastness in Brahman through the realisation of one’s identity with It gives rise to bliss and thoroughly removes the misery born of nescience, which one experiences (in the ignorant state).

334.shloka:
बाह्यानुसन्धिः परिवर्धयेत्फलं दुर्वासनामेव ततस्ततोऽधिकाम् ।
ज्ञात्वा विवेकैः परिहृत्य बाह्यं स्वात्मानुसन्धिं विदधीत नित्यम् ॥ ३३४ ॥
334.transliteration:
bāhyānusandhiḥ parivardhayetphalaṃ durvāsanāmeva tatastato'dhikām |
jñātvā vivekaiḥ parihṛtya bāhyaṃ svātmānusandhiṃ vidadhīta nityam || 334 ||
334.translation: The dwelling on external objects will only intensify its fruits, viz. furthering evil propensities, which grow worse and worse. Knowing this through discrimination, one should avoid external objects and constantly apply oneself to meditation on the Ātman.

335.shloka:
बाह्ये निरुद्धे मनसः प्रसन्नता मनःप्रसादे परमात्मदर्शनम् ।
तस्मिन्सुदृष्टे भवबन्धनाशो बहिर्निरोधः पदवी विमुक्तेः ॥ ३३५ ॥
335.transliteration:
bāhye niruddhe manasaḥ prasannatā manaḥprasāde paramātmadarśanam |
tasminsudṛṣṭe bhavabandhanāśo bahirnirodhaḥ padavī vimukteḥ || 335 ||
335.translation: When the external world is shut out, the mind is cheerful, and cheerfulness of the mind brings on the vision of the Paramātman. When It is perfectly realised, the chain of birth and death is broken. Hence the shutting out of the external world is the stepping- stone to Liberation.

336.shloka:
कः पण्डितः सन्सदसद्विवेकी श्रुतिप्रमाणः परमार्थदर्शी ।
जानन्हि कुर्यादसतोऽवलम्बं स्वपातहेतोः शिशुवन्मुमुक्षुः ॥ ३३६ ॥
336.transliteration:
kaḥ paṇḍitaḥ sansadasadvivekī śrutipramāṇaḥ paramārthadarśī |
jānanhi kuryādasato'valambaṃ svapātahetoḥ śiśuvanmumukṣuḥ || 336 ||
336.translation: Where is the man who being learned, able to discriminate the real from the unreal, believing the Vedas as authority, fixing his gaze on the Ātman, the Supreme Reality, and being a seeker after Liberation, will, like a child, consciously have recourse to the unreal (the universe) which will cause his fall?

337.shloka:
देहादिसंसक्तिमतो न मुक्तिः मुक्तस्य देहाद्यभिमत्यभावः ।
सुप्तस्य नो जागरणं न जाग्रतः स्वप्नस्तयोर्भिन्नगुणाश्रयत्वात् ॥ ३३७ ॥
337.transliteration:
dehādisaṃsaktimato na muktiḥ muktasya dehādyabhimatyabhāvaḥ |
suptasya no jāgaraṇaṃ na jāgrataḥ svapnastayorbhinnaguṇāśrayatvāt || 337 ||
337.translation: There is no Liberation for one who has attachment to the body etc., and the liberated man has no identification with the body etc. The sleeping man is not awake, nor is the waking man asleep, for these two states are contradictory in nature.

338.shloka:
अन्तर्बहिः स्वं स्थिरजङ्गमेषु ज्ञात्वात्मनाधारतया विलोक्य ।
त्यक्ताखिलोपाधिरखण्डरूपः पूर्णात्मना यः स्थित एष मुक्तः ॥ ३३८ ॥
338.transliteration:
antarbahiḥ svaṃ sthirajaṅgameṣu jñātvātmanādhāratayā vilokya |
tyaktākhilopādhirakhaṇḍarūpaḥ pūrṇātmanā yaḥ sthita eṣa muktaḥ || 338 ||
338.translation: He is free who, knowing through his mind the Self in moving and unmoving objects and observing It as their substratum, gives up all superimpositions and remains as the Absolute and the infinite Self.

339.shloka:
सर्वात्मना बन्धविमुक्तिहेतुः सर्वात्मभावान्न परोऽस्ति कश्चित् ।
दृश्याग्रहे सत्युपपद्यतेऽसौ सर्वात्मभावोऽस्य सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥ ३३९ ॥
339.transliteration:
sarvātmanā bandhavimuktihetuḥ sarvātmabhāvānna paro'sti kaścit |
dṛśyāgrahe satyupapadyate'sau sarvātmabhāvo'sya sadātmaniṣṭhayā || 339 ||
339.translation: To realise the whole universe as the Self is the means of getting rid of bondage. There is nothing higher than identifying the universe with the Self. One realises this state by excluding the objective world through steadfastness in the eternal Ātman.

340.shloka:
दृश्यस्याग्रहणं कथं नु घटते देहात्मना तिष्ठतो बाह्यार्थानुभवप्रसक्तमनसस्तत्तत्क्रियां कुर्वतः ।
संन्यस्ताखिलधर्मकर्मविषयैर्नित्यात्मनिष्ठापरैः तत्त्वज्ञैः करणीयमात्मनि सदानन्देच्छुभिर्यत्नतः ॥ ३४0 ॥
340.transliteration:
dṛśyasyāgrahaṇaṃ kathaṃ nu ghaṭate dehātmanā tiṣṭhato bāhyārthānubhavaprasaktamanasastattatkriyāṃ kurvataḥ |
saṃnyastākhiladharmakarmaviṣayairnityātmaniṣṭhāparaiḥ tattvajñaiḥ karaṇīyamātmani sadānandecchubhiryatnataḥ || 340 ||
340.translation: How is the exclusion of the objective world possible for one who lives identified with the body, whose mind is attached to the perception of external objects, and who performs various acts for that end? This exclusion should be carefully practised by sages who have renounced all kinds of duties and actions and objects, who are passionately devoted to the eternal Ātman, and who wish to possess an undying bliss.

341.shloka:
सर्वात्मसिद्धये भिक्षोः कृतश्रवणकर्मणः ।
समाधिं विदधात्येषा शान्तो दान्त इति श्रुतिः ॥ ३४१ ॥
341.transliteration:
sarvātmasiddhaye bhikṣoḥ kṛtaśravaṇakarmaṇaḥ |
samādhiṃ vidadhātyeṣā śānto dānta iti śrutiḥ || 341 ||
341.translation: To the Sannyasin who has gone through the act of hearing, the Shruti passage, 'Calm, self-controlled.' Etc., prescribes Samadhi for realising the identity of the universe with the Self.

342.shloka:
आरूढशक्तेरहमो विनाशः कर्तुन्न शक्य सहसापि पण्डितैः ।
ये निर्विकल्पाख्यसमाधिनिश्चलाः तानन्तरानन्तभवा हि वासनाः ॥ ३४२ ॥
342.transliteration:
ārūḍhaśakterahamo vināśaḥ kartunna śakya sahasāpi paṇḍitaiḥ |
ye nirvikalpākhyasamādhiniścalāḥ tānantarānantabhavā hi vāsanāḥ || 342 ||
342.translation: Even wise men cannot suddenly destroy egoism after it has once become strong, barring those who are perfectly calm through the Nirvikalpa Samadhi. Desires are verily the effect of innumerable births.

343.shloka:
अहंबुद्ध्यैव मोहिन्या योजयित्वावृतेर्बलात् ।
विक्षेपशक्तिः पुरुषं विक्षेपयति तद्गुणैः ॥ ३४३ ॥
343.transliteration:
ahaṃbuddhyaiva mohinyā yojayitvāvṛterbalāt |
vikṣepaśaktiḥ puruṣaṃ vikṣepayati tadguṇaiḥ || 343 ||
343.translation: The projecting power, through the aid of the veiling power, connects a man with the siren of an egoistic idea, and distracts him through the attributes of that.

344.shloka:
विक्षेपशक्तिविजयो विषमो विधातुं निःशेषमावरणशक्तिनिवृत्त्यभावे ।
दृग्दृश्ययोः स्फुटपयोजलवद्विभागे नश्येत्तदावरणमात्मनि च स्वभावात् निःसंशयेन भवति प्रतिबन्धशून्यो विक्षेपणं नहिं तदा यदि चेन्मृषार्थे ॥ ३४४ ॥
344.transliteration:
vikṣepaśaktivijayo viṣamo vidhātuṃ niḥśeṣamāvaraṇaśaktinivṛttyabhāve |
dṛgdṛśyayoḥ sphuṭapayojalavadvibhāge naśyettadāvaraṇamātmani ca svabhāvāt niḥsaṃśayena bhavati pratibandhaśūnyo vikṣepaṇaṃ nahiṃ tadā yadi cenmṛṣārthe || 344 ||
344.translation: It is extremely difficult to conquer the projecting power unless the veiling power is perfectly rooted out. And that covering over the Ātman naturally vanishes when the subject is perfectly distinguished from the objects, like milk from water. But the victory is undoubtedly (complete and) free from obstacles when there is no oscillation of the mind due to the unreal sense-objects.

345.shloka:
सम्यग्विवेकः स्फुटबोधजन्यो विभज्य दृग्दृश्यपदार्थतत्त्वम् ।
छिनत्ति मायाकृतमोहबन्धं यस्माद्विमुक्तस्तु पुनर्न संसृतिः ॥ ३४५ ॥
345.transliteration:
samyagvivekaḥ sphuṭabodhajanyo vibhajya dṛgdṛśyapadārthatattvam |
chinatti māyākṛtamohabandhaṃ yasmādvimuktastu punarna saṃsṛtiḥ || 345 ||
345.translation: Perfect discrimination brought on by direct realisation distinguishes the true nature of the subject from that of the object, and breaks the bond of delusion created by Māyā; and there is no more transmigration for one who has been freed from this.

346.shloka:
परावरैकत्वविवेकवन्हिः दहत्यविद्यागहनं ह्यशेषम् ।
किं स्यात्पुनः संसरणस्य बीजं अद्वैतभावं समुपेयुषोऽस्य ॥ ३४६ ॥
346.transliteration:
parāvaraikatvavivekavanhiḥ dahatyavidyāgahanaṃ hyaśeṣam |
kiṃ syātpunaḥ saṃsaraṇasya bījaṃ advaitabhāvaṃ samupeyuṣo'sya || 346 ||
346.translation: The knowledge of the identity of the Jiva and Brahman entirely consumes the impenetrable forest of Avidya or Nescience. For one who has realised the state of Oneness, is there any seed left for future transmigration?

347.translation: The veil that hides Truth vanishes only when the Reality is fully realised. (Thence follow) the destruction of false knowledge and the cessation of misery brought about by its distracting influence.

348.shloka:
एतत्त्रितयं दृष्टं सम्यग्रज्जुस्वरूपविज्ञानात् ।
तस्माद्वस्तुसतत्त्वं ज्ञातव्यं बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ॥ ३४८ ॥
348.transliteration:
etattritayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ samyagrajjusvarūpavijñānāt |
tasmādvastusatattvaṃ jñātavyaṃ bandhamuktaye viduṣā || 348 ||
348.translation: These three are observed in the case of a rope when its real nature is fully known. Therefore the wise man should know the real nature of things for the breaking of his bonds.

349.shloka:
अयोऽग्नियोगादिव सत्समन्वयान् मात्रादिरूपेण विजृम्भते धीः ।
तत्कार्यमेतद्द्वितयं यतो मृषा दृष्टं भ्रमस्वप्नमनोरथेषु ॥ ३४९ ॥
349.transliteration:
ततो विकाराः प्रकृतेरहंमुखा देहावसाना विषयाश्च सर्वे ।
क्षणेऽन्यथाभावितया ह्यमीषाम् असत्त्वमात्मा तु कदापि नान्यथा ॥ ३५0 ॥
349.translation: 349-350. Like iron manifesting as sparks through contact with fire, the Buddhi manifests itself as knower and known through the inherence of Brahman. As these two (knower and known), the effects of the Buddhi, are observed to be unreal in the case of delusion, dream and fancy, similarly, the modifications of the Prakriti, from egoism down to the body and all sense-objects are also unreal. Their unreality is verily due to their being subject to change every moment. But the Ātman never changes.

350.shloka:
नित्याद्वयाखण्डचिदेकरूपो बुद्ध्यादिसाक्षी सदसद्विलक्षणः ।
अहंपदप्रत्ययलक्षितार्थः प्रत्यक्सदानन्दघनः परात्मा ॥ ३५१ ॥
350.transliteration:
nityādvayākhaṇḍacidekarūpo buddhyādisākṣī sadasadvilakṣaṇaḥ |
ahaṃpadapratyayalakṣitārthaḥ pratyaksadānandaghanaḥ parātmā || 351 ||
350.translation: The Supreme Self is ever of the nature of eternal, indivisible knowledge, one without a second, the Witness of the Buddhi and the rest, distinct from the gross and subtle, the implied meaning of the term and idea 'I', the embodiment of inward, eternal bliss.

351.shloka:
इत्थं विपश्चित्सदसद्विभज्य निश्चित्य तत्त्वं निजबोधदृष्ट्या ।
ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधं तेभ्यो विमुक्तः स्वयमेव शाम्यति ॥ ३५२ ॥
351.transliteration:
itthaṃ vipaścitsadasadvibhajya niścitya tattvaṃ nijabodhadṛṣṭyā |
jñātvā svamātmānamakhaṇḍabodhaṃ tebhyo vimuktaḥ svayameva śāmyati || 352 ||
351.translation: The wise man, discriminating thus the real and the unreal, ascertaining the Truth through his illuminative insight, and realising his own Self which is Knowledge Absolute, gets rid of the obstructions and directly attains Peace.

352.translation: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

353.translation: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

354.shloka:
त्वमहमिदमितीयं कल्पना बुद्धिदोषात् प्रभवति परमात्मन्यद्वये निर्विशेषे ।
प्रविलसति समाधावस्य सर्वो विकल्पो विलयनमुपगच्छेद्वस्तुतत्त्वावधृत्या ॥ ३५४ ॥
354.transliteration:
tvamahamidamitīyaṃ kalpanā buddhidoṣāt prabhavati paramātmanyadvaye nirviśeṣe |
pravilasati samādhāvasya sarvo vikalpo vilayanamupagacchedvastutattvāvadhṛtyā || 354 ||
354.translation: Such imaginations as 'thou', 'I' or 'this' take place through the defects of the Buddhi. But when the Paramātman, the Absolute, the One without a second, manifests Itself in Samadhi, all such imaginations are dissolved for the aspirant, through the realisation of the truth of Brahman.

355.shloka:
शान्तो दान्तः परमुपरतः क्षान्तियुक्तः समाधिं कुर्वन्नित्यं कलयति यतिः स्वस्य सर्वात्मभावम् ।
तेनाविद्यातिमिरजनितान्साधु दग्ध्वा विकल्पान् ब्रह्माकृत्या निवसति सुखं निष्क्रियो निर्विकल्पः ॥ ३५५ ॥
355.transliteration:
śānto dāntaḥ paramuparataḥ kṣāntiyuktaḥ samādhiṃ kurvannityaṃ kalayati yatiḥ svasya sarvātmabhāvam |
tenāvidyātimirajanitānsādhu dagdhvā vikalpān brahmākṛtyā nivasati sukhaṃ niṣkriyo nirvikalpaḥ || 355 ||
355.translation: The Sannyasin, calm, self-controlled, perfectly retiring from the sense-world, forbearing, and devoting himself to the practice of Samadhi, always reflects on his own self being the Self of the whole universe. Destroying completely by this means the imaginations which are due to the gloom of ignorance, he lives blissfully as Brahman, free from action and the oscillations of the mind.

356.shloka:
समाहिता ये प्रविलाप्य बाह्यं श्रोत्रादि चेतः स्वमहं चिदात्मनि ।
त एव मुक्ता भवपाशबन्धैः नान्ये तु पारोक्ष्यकथाभिधायिनः ॥ ३५६ ॥
356.transliteration:
samāhitā ye pravilāpya bāhyaṃ śrotrādi cetaḥ svamahaṃ cidātmani |
ta eva muktā bhavapāśabandhaiḥ nānye tu pārokṣyakathābhidhāyinaḥ || 356 ||
356.translation: Those alone are free from the bondage of transmigration who, attaining Samadhi, have merged the objective world, the sense-organs, the mind, nay, the very ego, in the Ātman, the Knowledge Absolute – and none else, who but dabble in second-hand talks.

357.shloka:
उपाधिभेदात्स्वयमेव भिद्यते चोपाध्यपोहे स्वयमेव केवलः ।
तस्मादुपाधेर्विलयाय विद्वान् वसेत्सदाकल्पसमाधिनिष्ठया ॥ ३५७ ॥
357.transliteration:
upādhibhedātsvayameva bhidyate copādhyapohe svayameva kevalaḥ |
tasmādupādhervilayāya vidvān vasetsadākalpasamādhiniṣṭhayā || 357 ||
357.translation: Through the diversity of the supervening conditions (Upadhis), a man is apt to think of himself as also full of diversity; but with the removal of these he is again his own Self, the immutable. Therefore the wise man should ever devote himself to the practice of Nirvikalpa Samadhi, for the dissolution of the Upadhis.

358.shloka:
सति सक्तो नरो याति सद्भावं ह्येकनिष्ठया ।
कीटको भ्रमरं ध्यायन् भ्रमरत्वाय कल्पते ॥ ३५८ ॥
358.transliteration:
sati sakto naro yāti sadbhāvaṃ hyekaniṣṭhayā |
kīṭako bhramaraṃ dhyāyan bhramaratvāya kalpate || 358 ||
358.translation: The man who is attached to the Real becomes Real, through his one-pointed devotion. Just as the cockroach thinking intently on the Bhramara is transformed into a Bhramara.

359.shloka:
क्रियान्तरासक्तिमपास्य कीटको ध्यायन्नलित्वं ह्यलिभावमृच्छति ।
तथैव योगी परमात्मतत्त्वं ध्यात्वा समायाति तदेकनिष्ठया ॥ ३५९ ॥
359.transliteration:
kriyāntarāsaktimapāsya kīṭako dhyāyannalitvaṃ hyalibhāvamṛcchati |
tathaiva yogī paramātmatattvaṃ dhyātvā samāyāti tadekaniṣṭhayā || 359 ||
359.translation: Just as the cockroach, giving up the attachment to all other actions, thinks intently on the Bhramara and becomes transformed into that worm, exactly in the same manner the Yogi, meditating on the truth of the Paramātman, attains to It through his one- pointed devotion to that.

360.shloka:
अतीव सूक्ष्मं परमात्मतत्त्वं न स्थूलदृष्ट्या प्रतिपत्तुमर्हति ।
समाधिनात्यन्तसुसूक्ष्मवृत्या ज्ञातव्यमार्यैरतिशुद्धबुद्धिभिः ॥ ३६0 ॥
360.transliteration:
atīva sūkṣmaṃ paramātmatattvaṃ na sthūladṛṣṭyā pratipattumarhati |
samādhinātyantasusūkṣmavṛtyā jñātavyamāryairatiśuddhabuddhibhiḥ || 360 ||
360.translation: The truth of the Paramātman is extremely subtle, and cannot be reached by the gross outgoing tendency of the mind. It is only accessible to noble souls with perfectly pure minds, by means of Samadhi brought on by an extraordinary fineness of the mental state.

361.shloka:
यथा सुवर्णं पुटपाकशोधितं त्यक्त्वा मलं स्वात्मगुणं समृच्छति ।
तथा मनः सत्त्वरजस्तमोमलं ध्यानेन सन्त्यज्य समेति तत्त्वम् ॥ ३६१ ॥
361.transliteration:
yathā suvarṇaṃ puṭapākaśodhitaṃ tyaktvā malaṃ svātmaguṇaṃ samṛcchati |
tathā manaḥ sattvarajastamomalaṃ dhyānena santyajya sameti tattvam || 361 ||
361.translation: As gold purified by thorough heating on the fire gives up its impurities and attains to its own lustre, so the mind, through meditation, gives up its impurities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and attains to the reality of Brahman.

362.shloka:
निरन्तराभ्यासवशात्तदित्थं पक्वं मनो ब्रह्मणि लीयते यदा ।
तदा समाधिः सविकल्पवर्जितः स्वतोऽद्वयानन्दरसानुभावकः ॥ ३६२ ॥
362.transliteration:
nirantarābhyāsavaśāttaditthaṃ pakvaṃ mano brahmaṇi līyate yadā |
tadā samādhiḥ savikalpavarjitaḥ svato'dvayānandarasānubhāvakaḥ || 362 ||
362.translation: When the mind, thus purified by constant practice, is merged in Brahman, then Samadhi passes on from the Savikalpa to the Nirvikalpa stage, and leads directly to the realisation of the Bliss of Brahman, the One without a second.

363.shloka:
समाधिनानेन समस्तवासना ग्रन्थेर्विनाशोऽखिलकर्मनाशः ।
अन्तर्बहिः सर्वत एव सर्वदा स्वरूपविस्फूर्तिरयत्नतः स्यात् ॥ ३६३ ॥
363.transliteration:
samādhinānena samastavāsanā granthervināśo'khilakarmanāśaḥ |
antarbahiḥ sarvata eva sarvadā svarūpavisphūrtirayatnataḥ syāt || 363 ||
363.translation: By this Samadhi are destroyed all desires which are like knots, all work is at an end, and inside and out there takes place everywhere and always the spontaneous manifestation of one’s real nature.

364.shloka:
श्रुतेः शतगुणं विद्यान्मननं मननादपि ।
निदिंध्यासं लक्षगुणमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ॥ ३६४ ॥
364.transliteration:
śruteḥ śataguṇaṃ vidyānmananaṃ mananādapi |
nidiṃdhyāsaṃ lakṣaguṇamanantaṃ nirvikalpakam || 364 ||
364.translation: Reflection should be considered a hundred times superior to hearing, and meditation a hundred thousand times superior even to reflection, but the Nirvikalpa Samadhi is infinite in its results.

365.shloka:
निर्विकल्पकसमाधिना स्फुटं ब्रह्मतत्त्वमवगम्यते ध्रुवम् ।
नान्यथा चलतया मनोगतेः प्रत्ययान्तरविमिश्रितं भवेत् ॥ ३६५ ॥
365.transliteration:
nirvikalpakasamādhinā sphuṭaṃ brahmatattvamavagamyate dhruvam |
nānyathā calatayā manogateḥ pratyayāntaravimiśritaṃ bhavet || 365 ||
365.translation: By the Nirvikalpa Samadhi the truth of Brahman is clearly and definitely realised, but not otherwise, for then the mind, being unstable by nature, is apt to be mixed up with other perceptions.

366.shloka:
अतः समाधत्स्व यतेन्द्रियः सन् निरन्तरं शान्तमनाः प्रतीचि ।
विध्वंसय ध्वान्तमनाद्यविद्यया कृतं सदेकत्वविलोकनेन ॥ ३६६ ॥
366.transliteration:
ataḥ samādhatsva yatendriyaḥ san nirantaraṃ śāntamanāḥ pratīci |
vidhvaṃsaya dhvāntamanādyavidyayā kṛtaṃ sadekatvavilokanena || 366 ||
366.translation: Hence with the mind calm and the senses controlled always drown the mind in the Supreme Self that is within, and through the realisation of thy identity with that Reality destroy the darkness created by Nescience, which is without beginning.

367.shloka:
योगस्य प्रथमद्वारं वाङ्निरोधोऽपरिग्रहः ।
निराशा च निरीहा च नित्यमेकान्तशीलता ॥ ३६७ ॥
367.transliteration:
yogasya prathamadvāraṃ vāṅnirodho'parigrahaḥ |
nirāśā ca nirīhā ca nityamekāntaśīlatā || 367 ||
367.translation: The first steps to Yoga are control of speech, non-receiving of gifts, entertaining of no expectations, freedom from activity, and always living in a retired place.

368.shloka:
एकान्तस्थितिरिन्द्रियोपरमणे हेनुर्दमश्चेतसः संरोधे करणं शमेन विलयं यायादहंवासना ।
तेनानन्दरसानुभूतिरचला ब्राह्मी सदा योगिनः तस्माच्चित्तनिरोध एव सततं कार्यः प्रयत्नो मुनेः ॥ ३६८ ॥
368.transliteration:
ekāntasthitirindriyoparamaṇe henurdamaścetasaḥ saṃrodhe karaṇaṃ śamena vilayaṃ yāyādahaṃvāsanā |
tenānandarasānubhūtiracalā brāhmī sadā yoginaḥ tasmāccittanirodha eva satataṃ kāryaḥ prayatno muneḥ || 368 ||
368.translation: Living in a retired place serves to control the sense-organs, control of the senses helps to control the mind, through control of the mind egoism is destroyed; and this again gives the Yogi an unbroken realisation of the Bliss of Brahman. Therefore the man of reflection should always strive only to control the mind.

369.shloka:
वाचं नियच्छात्मनि तं नियच्छ बुद्धौ धियं यच्छ च बुद्धिसाक्षिणि ।
तं चापि पूर्णात्मनि निर्विकल्पे विलाप्य शान्तिं परमां भजस्व ॥ ३६९ ॥
369.transliteration:
vācaṃ niyacchātmani taṃ niyaccha buddhau dhiyaṃ yaccha ca buddhisākṣiṇi |
taṃ cāpi pūrṇātmani nirvikalpe vilāpya śāntiṃ paramāṃ bhajasva || 369 ||
369.translation: Restrain speech in the Manas, and restrain Manas in the Buddhi; this again restrain in the witness of Buddhi, and merging that also in the Infinite Absolute Self, attain to supreme Peace.

370.translation: The body, Prāṇas, organs, manas, Buddhi and the rest – with whichever of these supervening adjuncts the mind is associated, the Yogi is transformed, as it were, into that.

371.shloka:
तन्निवृत्त्या मुनेः सम्यक्सर्वोपरमणं सुखम् ।
संदृश्यते सदानन्दरसानुभवविप्लवः ॥ ३७१ ॥
371.transliteration:
tannivṛttyā muneḥ samyaksarvoparamaṇaṃ sukham |
saṃdṛśyate sadānandarasānubhavaviplavaḥ || 371 ||
371.translation: When this is stopped, the man of reflection is found to be easily detached from everything, and to get the experience of an abundance of everlasting Bliss.

372.shloka:
अन्तस्त्यागो बहिस्त्यागो विरक्तस्यैव युज्यते ।
त्यजत्यन्तर्बहिःसङ्गं विरक्तस्तु मुमुक्षया ॥ ३७२ ॥
372.transliteration:
antastyāgo bahistyāgo viraktasyaiva yujyate |
tyajatyantarbahiḥsaṅgaṃ viraktastu mumukṣayā || 372 ||
372.translation: It is the man of dispassion (Vairāgya) who is fit for this internal as well as external renunciation; for the dispassionate man, out of the desire to be free, relinquishes both internal and external attachment.

373.shloka:
बहिस्तु विषयैः सङ्गं तथान्तरहमादिभिः ।
विरक्त एव शक्नोति त्यक्तुं ब्रह्मणि निष्ठितः ॥ ३७३ ॥
373.transliteration:
bahistu viṣayaiḥ saṅgaṃ tathāntarahamādibhiḥ |
virakta eva śaknoti tyaktuṃ brahmaṇi niṣṭhitaḥ || 373 ||
373.translation: It is only the dispassionate man who, being thoroughly grounded in Brahman, can give up the external attachment to the sense-objects and the internal attachment for egoism etc.

374.shloka:
वैराग्यबोधौ पुरुषस्य पक्षिवत् पक्षौ विजानीहि विचक्षण त्वम् ।
विमुक्तिसौधाग्रलताधिरोहणं ताभ्यां विना नान्यतरेण सिध्यति ॥ ३७४ ॥
374.transliteration:
vairāgyabodhau puruṣasya pakṣivat pakṣau vijānīhi vicakṣaṇa tvam |
vimuktisaudhāgralatādhirohaṇaṃ tābhyāṃ vinā nānyatareṇa sidhyati || 374 ||
374.translation: Know, O wise man, dispassion and discrimination to be like the two wings of a bird in the case of an aspirant. Unless both are there, none can, with the help of either one, reach the creeper of Liberation that grows, as it were, on the top of an edifice.

375.shloka:
अत्यन्तवैराग्यवतः समाधिः समाहितस्यैव दृढप्रबोधः ।
प्रबुद्धतत्त्वस्य हि बन्धमुक्तिः मुक्तात्मनो नित्यसुखानुभूतिः ॥ ३७५ ॥
375.transliteration:
atyantavairāgyavataḥ samādhiḥ samāhitasyaiva dṛḍhaprabodhaḥ |
prabuddhatattvasya hi bandhamuktiḥ muktātmano nityasukhānubhūtiḥ || 375 ||
375.translation: The extremely dispassionate man alone has Samadhi, and the man of Samadhi alone gets steady realisation; the man who has realised the Truth is alone free from bondage, and the free soul only experiences eternal Bliss.

376.shloka:
वैराग्यान्न परं सुखस्य जनकं पश्यामि वश्यात्मनः तच्चेच्छुद्धतरात्मबोधसहितं स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यधुक् ।
एतद्द्वारमजस्रमुक्तियुवतेर्यस्मात्त्वमस्मात्परं सर्वत्रास्पृहया सदात्मनि सदा प्रज्ञां कुरु श्रेयसे ॥ ३७६ ॥
376.transliteration:
vairāgyānna paraṃ sukhasya janakaṃ paśyāmi vaśyātmanaḥ taccecchuddhatarātmabodhasahitaṃ svārājyasāmrājyadhuk |
etaddvāramajasramuktiyuvateryasmāttvamasmātparaṃ sarvatrāspṛhayā sadātmani sadā prajñāṃ kuru śreyase || 376 ||
376.translation: For the man of self-control I do not find any better instrument of happiness than dispassion, and if that is coupled with a highly pure realisation of the Self, it conduces to the suzerainty of absolute Independence; and since this is the gateway to the damsel of everlasting liberation, therefore for thy welfare, be dispassionate both internally and externally, and always fix thy mind on the eternal Self.

377.shloka:
आशां छिन्द्धि विषोपमेषु विषयेष्वेषैव मृत्योः कृतिस् त्यक्त्वा जातिकुलाश्रमेष्वभिमतिं मुञ्चातिदूरात्क्रियाः ।
देहादावसति त्यजात्मधिषणां प्रज्ञां कुरुष्वात्मनि त्वं द्रष्टास्यमनोऽसि निर्द्वयपरं ब्रह्मासि यद्वस्तुतः ॥ ३७७ ॥
377.transliteration:
āśāṃ chinddhi viṣopameṣu viṣayeṣveṣaiva mṛtyoḥ kṛtis tyaktvā jātikulāśrameṣvabhimatiṃ muñcātidūrātkriyāḥ |
dehādāvasati tyajātmadhiṣaṇāṃ prajñāṃ kuruṣvātmani tvaṃ draṣṭāsyamano'si nirdvayaparaṃ brahmāsi yadvastutaḥ || 377 ||
377.translation: Sever thy craving for the sense-objects, which are like poison, for it is the very image of death, and giving up thy pride of caste, family and order of life, fling actions to a distance. Give up thy identification with such unreal things as the body, and fix thy mind on the Ātman. For thou art really the Witness, Brahman, unshackled by the mind, the One without a second, and Supreme.

378.shloka:
लक्ष्ये ब्रह्मणि मानसं दृढतरं संस्थाप्य बाह्येन्द्रियं स्वस्थाने विनिवेश्य निश्चलतनुश्चोपेक्ष्य देहस्थितिम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमुपेत्य तन्मायातया चाखण्डवृत्त्यानिशं ब्रह्मानन्दरसं पिबात्मनि मुदा शून्यैः किमन्यैर्भृशम् ॥ ३७८ ॥
378.transliteration:
lakṣye brahmaṇi mānasaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ saṃsthāpya bāhyendriyaṃ svasthāne viniveśya niścalatanuścopekṣya dehasthitim |
brahmātmaikyamupetya tanMāyātayā cākhaṇḍavṛttyāniśaṃ brahmānandarasaṃ pibātmani mudā śūnyaiḥ kimanyairbhṛśam || 378 ||
378.translation: Fixing the mind firmly on the Ideal, Brahman, and restraining the external organs in their respective centres; with the body held steady and taking no thought for its maintenance; attaining identity with Brahman and being one with It – always drink joyfully of the Bliss of Brahman in thy own Self, without a break. What is the use of other things which are entirely hollow?

379.shloka:
अनात्मचिन्तनं त्यक्त्वा कश्मलं दुःखकारणम् ।
चिन्तयात्मानमानन्दरूपं यन्मुक्तिकारणम् ॥ ३७९ ॥
379.transliteration:
anātmacintanaṃ tyaktvā kaśmalaṃ duḥkhakāraṇam |
cintayātmānamānandarūpaṃ yanmuktikāraṇam || 379 ||
379.translation: Giving up the thought of the non-Self which is evil and productive of misery, think of the Self, the Bliss Absolute, which conduces to Liberation.

380.shloka:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरशेषसाक्षी विज्ञानकोशो विलसत्यजस्रम् ।
लक्ष्यं विधायैनमसद्विलक्षणम् अखण्डवृत्त्यात्मतयानुभावय ॥ ३८0 ॥
380.transliteration:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiraśeṣasākṣī vijñānakośo vilasatyajasram |
lakṣyaṃ vidhāyainamasadvilakṣaṇam akhaṇḍavṛttyātmatayānubhāvaya || 380 ||
380.translation: Here shines eternally the Ātman, the Self-effulgent Witness of everything, which has the Buddhi for Its seat. Making this Ātman which is distinct from the unreal, the goal, meditate on It as thy own Self, excluding all other thought.

381.translation: Reflecting on this Ātman continuously and without any foreign thought intervening, one must distinctly realise It to be one’s real Self.

382.shloka:
अत्रात्मत्वं दृढीकुर्वन्नहमादिषु संत्यजन् ।
उदासीनतया तेषु तिष्ठेत्स्फुटघटादिवत् ॥ ३८२ ॥
382.transliteration:
atrātmatvaṃ dṛḍhīkurvannahamādiṣu saṃtyajan |
udāsīnatayā teṣu tiṣṭhetsphuṭaghaṭādivat || 382 ||
382.translation: Strengthening one’s identification with This, and giving up that with egoism and the rest, one must live without any concern for them, as if they were trifling things, like a cracked jar or the like.

383.shloka:
विशुद्धमन्तःकरणं स्वरूपे निवेश्य साक्षिण्यवबोधमात्रे ।
शनैः शनैर्निश्चलतामुपानयन् पूर्णं स्वमेवानुविलोकयेत्ततः ॥ ३८३ ॥
383.transliteration:
viśuddhamantaḥkaraṇaṃ svarūpe niveśya sākṣiṇyavabodhamātre |
śanaiḥ śanairniścalatāmupānayan pūrṇaṃ svamevānuvilokayettataḥ || 383 ||
383.translation: Fixing the purified mind in the Self, the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute, and slowly making it still, one must then realise one’s own infinite Self.

384.translation: One should behold the Ātman, the Indivisible and Infinite, free from all limiting adjuncts such as the body, organs, Prāṇas, Manas and egoism, which are creations of one’s own ignorance – like the infinite sky.

385.shloka:
घटकलशकुसूलसूचिमुख्यैः गगनमुपाधिशतैर्विमुक्तमेकम् ।
भवति न विविधं तथैव शुद्धं परमहमादिविमुक्तमेकमेव ॥ ३८५ ॥
385.transliteration:
ghaṭakalaśakusūlasūcimukhyaiḥ gaganamupādhiśatairvimuktamekam |
bhavati na vividhaṃ tathaiva śuddhaṃ paramahamādivimuktamekameva || 385 ||
385.translation: The sky, divested of the hundreds of limiting adjuncts such as a jar, a pitcher, a receptacle for grains or a needle, is one, and not diverse; exactly in a similar way the pure Brahman, when divested of egoism etc., is verily One.

386.shloka:
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्ता मृषामात्रा उपाधयः ।
ततः पूर्णं स्वमात्मानं पश्येदेकात्मना स्थितम् ॥ ३८६ ॥
386.transliteration:
brahmādistambaparyantā mṛṣāmātrā upādhayaḥ |
tataḥ pūrṇaṃ svamātmānaṃ paśyedekātmanā sthitam || 386 ||
386.translation: The limiting adjuncts from Brahma down to a clump of grass are all wholly unreal. Therefore one should realise one’s own Infinite Self as the only Principle.

387.shloka:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पितं तद्विवेके तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
भ्रान्तेर्नाशे भाति दृष्टाहितत्त्वं रज्जुस्तद्वद्विश्वमात्मस्वरूपम् ॥ ३८७ ॥
387.transliteration:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpitaṃ tadviveke tattanmātraṃ naiva tasmādvibhinnam |
bhrānternāśe bhāti dṛṣṭāhitattvaṃ rajjustadvadviśvamātmasvarūpam || 387 ||
387.translation: That in which something is imagined to exist through error, is, when rightly discriminated, that thing itself, and not distinct from it. When the error is gone, the reality about the snake falsely perceived becomes the rope. Similarly the universe is in reality the Ātman.

388.shloka:
स्वयं ब्रह्मा स्वयं विष्णुः स्वयमिन्द्रः स्वयं शिवः ।
स्वयं विश्वमिदं सर्वं स्वस्मादन्यन्न किंचन ॥ ३८८ ॥
388.transliteration:
svayaṃ brahmā svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ svayamindraḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ |
svayaṃ viśvamidaṃ sarvaṃ svasmādanyanna kiṃcana || 388 ||
388.translation: The Self is Brahma, the Self is Vishnu, the Self is Indra, the Self is Shiva; the Self is all this universe. Nothing exists except the Self.

389.shloka:
अन्तः स्वयं चापि बहिः स्वयं च स्वयं पुरस्तात्स्वयमेव पश्चात् ।
स्वयं ह्यावाच्यां स्वयमप्युदीच्यां तथोपरिष्टात्स्वयमप्यधस्तात् ॥ ३८९ ॥
389.transliteration:
antaḥ svayaṃ cāpi bahiḥ svayaṃ ca svayaṃ purastātsvayameva paścāt |
svayaṃ hyāvācyāṃ svayamapyudīcyāṃ tathopariṣṭātsvayamapyadhastāt || 389 ||
389.translation: The Self is within, and the Self is without; the Self is before and the Self is behind; the Self is in the south, and the Self is in the north; the Self likewise is above as also below.

390.shloka:
तरङ्गफेनभ्रमबुद्बुदादि सर्वं स्वरूपेण जलं यथा तथा ।
चिदेव देहाद्यहमन्तमेतत् सर्वं चिदेवैकरसं विशुद्धम् ॥ ३९0 ॥
390.transliteration:
taraṅgaphenabhramabudbudādi sarvaṃ svarūpeṇa jalaṃ yathā tathā |
cideva dehādyahamantametat sarvaṃ cidevaikarasaṃ viśuddham || 390 ||
390.translation: As the wave, the foam, the whirlpool, the bubble, etc., are all in essence but water, similarly the Chit (Knowledge Absolute) is all this, from the body up to egoism. Everything is verily the Chit, homogeneous and pure.

391.shloka:
सदेवेदं सर्वं जगदवगतं वाङ्मनसयोः सतोऽन्यन्नास्त्येव प्रकृतिपरसीम्नि स्थितवतः ।
पृथक्किं मृत्स्नायाः कलशघटकुम्भाद्यवगतं वदत्येष भ्रान्तस्त्वमहमिति मायामदिरया ॥ ३९१ ॥
391.transliteration:
sadevedaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavagataṃ vāṅmanasayoḥ sato'nyannāstyeva prakṛtiparasīmni sthitavataḥ |
pṛthakkiṃ mṛtsnāyāḥ kalaśaghaṭakumbhādyavagataṃ vadatyeṣa bhrāntastvamahamiti māyāmadirayā || 391 ||
391.translation: All this universe known through speech and mind is nothing but Brahman; there is nothing besides Brahman, which exists beyond the utmost range of the Prakriti. Are the pitcher, jug, jar, etc., known to be distinct from the clay of which they are composed? It is the deluded man who talks of 'thou' and 'I', as an effect of the wine of Māyā.

392.shloka:
क्रियासमभिहारेण यत्र नान्यदिति श्रुतिः ।
ब्रवीति द्वैतराहित्यं मिथ्याध्यासनिवृत्तये ॥ ३९२ ॥
392.transliteration:
kriyāsamabhihāreṇa yatra nānyaditi śrutiḥ |
bravīti dvaitarāhityaṃ mithyādhyāsanivṛttaye || 392 ||
392.translation: The Śruti, in the passage, 'Where one sees nothing else', etc., declares by an accumulation of verbs the absence of duality, in order to remove the false superimpositions.

393.shloka:
आकाशवन्निर्मलनिर्विकल्पं निःसीमनिःस्पन्दननिर्विकारम् ।
अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यमद्वयं स्वयं परं ब्रह्म किमस्ति बोध्यम् ॥ ३९३ ॥
393.transliteration:
ākāśavannirmalanirvikalpaṃ niḥsīmaniḥspandananirvikāram |
antarbahiḥśūnyamananyamadvayaṃ svayaṃ paraṃ brahma kimasti bodhyam || 393 ||
393.translation: The Supreme Brahman is, like the sky, pure, absolute, infinite, motionless and changeless, devoid of interior or exterior, the One Existence, without a second, and is one’s own Self. Is there any other object of knowledge?

394.shloka:
वक्तव्यं किमु विद्यतेऽत्र बहुधा ब्रह्मैव जीवः स्वयं ब्रह्मैतज्जगदाततं नु सकलं ब्रह्माद्वितीयं श्रुतिः ।
ब्रह्मैवाहमिति प्रबुद्धमतयः संत्यक्तबाह्याः स्फुटं ब्रह्मीभूय वसन्ति सन्ततचिदानन्दात्मनैतद्ध्रुवम् ॥ ३९४ ॥
394.transliteration:
vaktavyaṃ kimu vidyate'tra bahudhā brahmaiva jīvaḥ svayaṃ brahmaitajjagadātataṃ nu sakalaṃ brahmādvitīyaṃ śrutiḥ |
brahmaivāhamiti prabuddhamatayaḥ saṃtyaktabāhyāḥ sphuṭaṃ brahmībhūya vasanti santatacidānandātmanaitaddhruvam || 394 ||
394.translation: What is the use of dilating on this subject? The Jīva is no other than Brahman; this whole extended universe is Brahman Itself; the Śruti inculcates the Brahman without a second; and it is an indubitable fact that people of enlightened minds who know their identity with Brahman and have given up their connection with the objective world, live palpably unifold with Brahman as Eternal Knowledge and Bliss.

395.shloka:
जहि मलमायाकोशेऽहंधियोत्थापिताशां प्रसभमनिलकल्पे लिङ्गदेहेऽपि पश्चात् ।
निगमगदितकीर्तिं नित्यमानन्दमूर्तिं स्वयमिति परिचीय ब्रह्मरूपेण तिष्ठ ॥ ३९५ ॥
395.transliteration:
jahi malaMāyākośe'haṃdhiyotthāpitāśāṃ prasabhamanilakalpe liṅgadehe'pi paścāt |
nigamagaditakīrtiṃ nityamānandamūrtiṃ svayamiti paricīya brahmarūpeṇa tiṣṭha || 395 ||
395.translation: (First) destroy the hopes raised by egoism in this filthy gross body, then do the same forcibly with the air-like subtle body; and realising Brahman, the embodiment of eternal Bliss – whose glories the Scriptures proclaim – as thy own Self, live as Brahman.

396.shloka:
शवाकारं यावद्भजति मनुजस्तावदशुचिः परेभ्यः स्यात्क्लेशो जननमरणव्याधिनिलयः ।
यदात्मानं शुद्धं कलयति शिवाकारमचलम् तदा तेभ्यो मुक्तो भवति हि तदाह श्रुतिरपि ॥ ३९६ ॥
396.transliteration:
śavākāraṃ yāvadbhajati manujastāvadaśuciḥ parebhyaḥ syātkleśo jananamaraṇavyādhinilayaḥ |
yadātmānaṃ śuddhaṃ kalayati śivākāramacalam tadā tebhyo mukto bhavati hi tadāha śrutirapi || 396 ||
396.translation: So long as man has any regard for this corpse-like body, he is impure, and suffers from his enemies as also from birth, death and disease; but when he thinks of himself as pure, as the essence of good and immovable, he assuredly becomes free from them; the Śrutis also say this.

397.translation: By the elimination of all apparent existences superimposed on the soul, the supreme Brahman, Infinite, the One without a second and beyond action, remains as Itself.

398.shloka:
समाहितायां सति चित्तवृत्तौ परात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
न दृश्यते कश्चिदयं विकल्पः प्रजल्पमात्रः परिशिष्यते यतः ॥ ३९८ ॥
398.transliteration:
samāhitāyāṃ sati cittavṛttau parātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
na dṛśyate kaścidayaṃ vikalpaḥ prajalpamātraḥ pariśiṣyate yataḥ || 398 ||
398.translation: When the mind-functions are merged in the Paramātman, the Brahman, the Absolute, none of this phenomenal world is seen, whence it is reduced to mere talk.

399.shloka:
असत्कल्पो विकल्पोऽयं विश्वमित्येकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ३९९ ॥
399.transliteration:
asatkalpo vikalpo'yaṃ viśvamityekavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 399 ||
399.translation: In the One Entity (Brahman) the conception of the universe is a mere phantom. Whence can there be any diversity in That which is changeless, formless and Absolute?

400.shloka:
द्रष्टुदर्शनदृश्यादिभावशून्यैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४00 ॥
400.transliteration:
draṣṭudarśanadṛśyādibhāvaśūnyaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 400 ||
400.translation: In the One Entity devoid of the concepts of seer, seeing and seen – which is changeless, formless and Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?

401.shloka:
कल्पार्णव इवात्यन्तपरिपूर्णैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४0१ ॥
401.transliteration:
kalpārṇava ivātyantaparipūrṇaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 401 ||
401.translation: In the One Entity which is changeless, formless and Absolute, and which is perfectly all-pervading and motionless like the ocean after the dissolution of the universe, whence can there be any diversity?

402.shloka:
तेजसीव तमो यत्र प्रलीनं भ्रान्तिकारणम् ।
अद्वितीये परे तत्त्वे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४0२ ॥
402.transliteration:
tejasīva tamo yatra pralīnaṃ bhrāntikāraṇam |
advitīye pare tattve nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 402 ||
402.translation: Where the root of delusion is dissolved like darkness in light – in the supreme Reality, the One without a second, the Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?

403.shloka:
एकात्मके परे तत्त्वे भेदवार्ता कथं वसेत् ।
सुषुप्तौ सुखमात्रायां भेदः केनावलोकितः ॥ ४0३ ॥
403.transliteration:
ekātmake pare tattve bhedavārtā kathaṃ vaset |
suṣuptau sukhamātrāyāṃ bhedaḥ kenāvalokitaḥ || 403 ||
403.translation: How can the talk of diversity apply to the Supreme Reality which is one and homogeneous? Who has ever observed diversity in the unmixed bliss of the state of profound sleep?

404.shloka:
न ह्यस्ति विश्वं परतत्त्वबोधात् सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
कालत्रये नाप्यहिरीक्षितो गुणे न ह्यम्बुबिन्दुर्मृगतृष्णिकायाम् ॥ ४0४ ॥
404.transliteration:
na hyasti viśvaṃ paratattvabodhāt sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
kālatraye nāpyahirīkṣito guṇe na hyambubindurmṛgatṛṣṇikāyām || 404 ||
404.translation: Even before the realisation of the highest Truth, the universe does not exist in the Absolute Brahman, the Essence of Existence. In none of the three states of time is the snake ever observed in the rope, nor a drop of water in the mirage.

405.shloka:
मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः ।
इति ब्रूते श्रुतिः साक्षात्सुषुप्तावनुभूयते ॥ ४0५ ॥
405.transliteration:
māyāmātramidaṃ dvaitamadvaitaṃ paramārthataḥ |
iti brūte śrutiḥ sākṣātsuṣuptāvanubhūyate || 405 ||
405.translation: The Śrutis themselves declare that this dualistic universe is but a delusion from the standpoint of Absolute Truth. This is also experienced in the state of dreamless sleep.

406.shloka:
अनन्यत्वमधिष्ठानादारोप्यस्य निरीक्षितम् ।
पण्डितै रज्जुसर्पादौ विकल्पो भ्रान्तिजीवनः ॥ ४0६ ॥
406.transliteration:
ananyatvamadhiṣṭhānādāropyasya nirīkṣitam |
paṇḍitai rajjusarpādau vikalpo bhrāntijīvanaḥ || 406 ||
406.translation: That which is superimposed upon something else is observed by the wise to be identical with the substratum, as in the case of the rope appearing as the snake. The apparent difference depends solely on error.

407.shloka:
चित्तमूलो विकल्पोऽयं चित्ताभावे न कश्चन ।
अतश्चित्तं समाधेहि प्रत्यग्रूपे परात्मनि ॥ ४0७ ॥
407.transliteration:
cittamūlo vikalpo'yaṃ cittābhāve na kaścana |
ataścittaṃ samādhehi pratyagrūpe parātmani || 407 ||
407.translation: This apparent universe has its root in the mind, and never persists after the mind is annihilated. Therefore dissolve the mind by concentrating it on the Supreme Self, which is thy inmost Essence.

408.shloka:
किमपि सततबोधं केवलानन्दरूपं निरुपममतिवेलं नित्यमुक्तं निरीहम् ।
निरवधिगगनाभं निष्कलं निर्विकल्पं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४0८ ॥
408.transliteration:
kimapi satatabodhaṃ kevalānandarūpaṃ nirupamamativelaṃ nityamuktaṃ nirīham |
niravadhigaganābhaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 408 ||
408.translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is something of the nature of eternal Knowledge and absolute Bliss, which has no exemplar, which transcends all limitations, is ever free and without activity, and which is like the limitless sky, indivisible and absolute.

409.shloka:
प्रकृतिविकृतिशून्यं भावनातीतभावं समरसमसमानं मानसं बन्धदूरम् ।
निगमवचनसिद्धं नित्यमस्मत्प्रसिद्धं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४0९ ॥
409.transliteration:
prakṛtivikṛtiśūnyaṃ bhāvanātītabhāvaṃ samarasamasamānaṃ mānasaṃ bandhadūram |
nigamavacanasiddhaṃ nityamasmatprasiddhaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 409 ||
409.translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is devoid of the ideas of cause and effect, which is the Reality beyond all imaginations, homogeneous, matchless, beyond the range of proofs, established by the pronouncements of the Vedas, and ever familiar to us as the sense of the ego.

410.shloka:
अजरममरमस्ताभाववस्तुस्वरूपं स्तिमितसलिलराशिप्रख्यमाख्याविहीनम् ।
शमितगुणविकारं शाश्वतं शान्तमेकं हृदि कलयति विद्वान् ब्रह्म पूर्णं समाधौ ॥ ४१0 ॥
410.transliteration:
ajaramamaramastābhāvavastusvarūpaṃ stimitasalilarāśiprakhyamākhyāvihīnam |
śamitaguṇavikāraṃ śāśvataṃ śāntamekaṃ hṛdi kalayati vidvān brahma pūrṇaṃ samādhau || 410 ||
410.translation: The wise man realises in his heart, through Samadhi, the Infinite Brahman, which is undecaying and immortal, the positive Entity which precludes all negations, which resembles the placid ocean and is without a name, in which there are neither merits nor demerits, and which is eternal, pacified and One.

411.shloka:
समाहितान्तःकरणः स्वरूपे विलोकयात्मानमखण्डवैभवम् ।
विच्छिन्द्धि बन्धं भवगन्धगन्धितं यत्नेन पुंस्त्वं सफलीकुरुष्व ॥ ४११
411.transliteration:
samāhitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ svarūpe vilokayātmānamakhaṇḍavaibhavam |
vicchinddhi bandhaṃ bhavagandhagandhitaṃ yatnena puṃstvaṃ saphalīkuruṣva || 411
411.translation: With the mind restrained in Samadhi, behold in thy self the Ātman, of infinite glory, cut off thy bondage strengthened by the impressions of previous births, and carefully attain the consummation of thy birth as a human being.

412.shloka:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तं सच्चिदानन्दमद्वयम् ।
भावयात्मानमात्मस्थं न भूयः कल्पसेऽध्वने ॥ ४१२ ॥
412.transliteration:
sarvopādhivinirmuktaṃ saccidānandamadvayam |
bhāvayātmānamātmasthaṃ na bhūyaḥ kalpase'dhvane || 412 ||
412.translation: Meditate on the Ātman, which resides in thee, which is devoid of all limiting adjuncts, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thou shalt no more come under the round of births and deaths.

413.shloka:
छायेव पुंसः परिदृश्यमान् माभासरूपेण फलानुभूत्या ।
शरीरमाराच्छववन्निरस्तं पुनर्न संधत्त इदं महात्मा ॥ ४१३ ॥
413.transliteration:
chāyeva puṃsaḥ paridṛśyamān mābhāsarūpeṇa phalānubhūtyā |
śarīramārācchavavannirastaṃ punarna saṃdhatta idaṃ mahātmā || 413 ||
413.translation: After the body has once been cast off to a distance like a corpse, the sage never more attaches himself to it, though it is visible as an appearance, like the shadow of a man, owing to the experience of the effects of past deeds.

414.shloka:
सततविमलबोधानन्दरूपं समेत्य त्यज जडमलरूपोपाधिमेतं सुदूरे ।
अथ पुनरपि नैष स्मर्यतां वान्तवस्तु स्मरणविषयभूतं पल्पते कुत्सनाय ॥ ४१४ ॥
414.transliteration:
satatavimalabodhānandarūpaṃ sametya tyaja jaḍamalarūpopādhimetaṃ sudūre |
atha punarapi naiṣa smaryatāṃ vāntavastu smaraṇaviṣayabhūtaṃ palpate kutsanāya || 414 ||
414.translation: Realising the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss, throw far away this limitation of a body, which is inert and filthy by nature. Then remember it no more, for something that has been vomited excites but disgust when called in memory.

415.shloka:
समूलमेतत्परिदाह्य वन्हौ सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
ततः स्वयं नित्यविशुद्धबोधा नन्दात्मना तिष्ठति विद्वरिष्ठः ॥ ४१५ ॥
415.transliteration:
samūlametatparidāhya vanhau sadātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
tataḥ svayaṃ nityaviśuddhabodhā nandātmanā tiṣṭhati vidvariṣṭhaḥ || 415 ||
415.translation: Burning all this, with its very root, in the fire of Brahman, the Eternal and Absolute Self, the truly wise man thereafter remains alone, as the Ātman, the eternal, pure Knowledge and Bliss.

416.shloka:
प्रारब्धसूत्रग्रथितं शरीरं प्रयातु वा तिष्ठतु गोरिव स्रक् ।
न तत्पुनः पश्यति तत्त्ववेत्ता (आ)नन्दात्मनि ब्रह्मणि लीनवृत्तिः ॥ ४१६ ॥
416.transliteration:
prārabdhasūtragrathitaṃ śarīraṃ prayātu vā tiṣṭhatu goriva srak |
na tatpunaḥ paśyati tattvavettā (ā)nandātmani brahmaṇi līnavṛttiḥ || 416 ||
416.translation: The knower of Truth does no more care whether this body, spun out by the threads of Prārabdha work, falls or remains – like the garland on a cow – for his mind-functions are at rest in the Brahman, the Essence of Bliss.

417.shloka:
अखण्डानन्दमात्मानं विज्ञाय स्वस्वरूपतः ।
किमिच्छन् कस्य वा हेतोर्देहं पुष्णाति तत्त्ववित् ॥ ४१७ ॥
417.transliteration:
akhaṇḍānandamātmānaṃ vijñāya svasvarūpataḥ |
kimicchan kasya vā hetordehaṃ puṣṇāti tattvavit || 417 ||
417.translation: Realising the Ātman, the Infinite Bliss, as his very Self, with what object, or for whom, should the knower of Truth cherish the body.

418.shloka:
संसिद्धस्य फलं त्वेतज्जीवन्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ।
बहिरन्तः सदानन्दरसास्वादनमात्मनि ॥ ४१८ ॥
418.transliteration:
saṃsiddhasya phalaṃ tvetajjīvanmuktasya yoginaḥ |
bahirantaḥ sadānandarasāsvādanamātmani || 418 ||
418.translation: The Yogi who has attained perfection and is liberated-in-life gets this as result – he enjoys eternal Bliss in his mind, internally as well as externally.

419.shloka:
वैराग्यस्य फलं बोधो बोधस्योपरतिः फलम् ।
स्वानन्दानुभवाच्छान्तिरेषैवोपरतेः फलम् ॥ ४१९ ॥
419.transliteration:
vairāgyasya phalaṃ bodho bodhasyoparatiḥ phalam |
svānandānubhavācchāntireṣaivoparateḥ phalam || 419 ||
419.translation: The result of dispassion is knowledge, that of Knowledge is withdrawal from sense-pleasures, which leads to the experience of the Bliss of the Self, whence follows Peace.

420.shloka:
यद्युत्तरोत्तराभावः पूर्वपूर्वन्तु निष्फलम् ।
निवृत्तिः परमा तृप्तिरानन्दोऽनुपमः स्वतः ॥ ४२0 ॥
420.transliteration:
yadyuttarottarābhāvaḥ pūrvapūrvantu niṣphalam |
nivṛttiḥ paramā tṛptirānando'nupamaḥ svataḥ || 420 ||
420.translation: If there is an absence of the succeeding stages, the preceding ones are futile. (When the series is perfect) the cessation of the objective world, extreme satisfaction, and matchless bliss follow as a matter of course.

421.shloka:
दृष्टदुःखेष्वनुद्वेगो विद्यायाः प्रस्तुतं फलम् ।
यत्कृतं भ्रान्तिवेलायां नाना कर्म जुगुप्सितम् पश्चान्नरो विवेकेन तत्कथं कर्तुमर्हति ॥ ४२१ ॥
421.transliteration:
dṛṣṭaduḥkheṣvanudvego vidyāyāḥ prastutaṃ phalam |
yatkṛtaṃ bhrāntivelāyāṃ nānā karma jugupsitam paścānnaro vivekena tatkathaṃ kartumarhati || 421 ||
421.translation: Being unruffled by earthly troubles is the result in question of knowledge. How can a man who did various loathsome deeds during the state of delusion, commit the same afterwards, possessed of discrimination?

422.shloka:
विद्याफलं स्यादसतो निवृत्तिः प्रवृत्तिरज्ञानफलं तदीक्षितम् ।
तज्ज्ञाज्ञयोर्यन्मृगतृष्णिकादौ नोचेद्विदां दृष्टफलं किमस्मात् ॥ ४२२ ॥
422.transliteration:
vidyāphalaṃ syādasato nivṛttiḥ pravṛttirajñānaphalaṃ tadīkṣitam |
tajjñājñayoryanmṛgatṛṣṇikādau nocedvidāṃ dṛṣṭaphalaṃ kimasmāt || 422 ||
422.translation: The result of knowledge should be the turning away from unreal things, while attachment to these is the result of ignorance. This is observed in the case of one who knows a mirage and things of that sort, and one who does not. Otherwise, what other tangible result do the knowers of Brahman obtain?

423.shloka:
अज्ञानहृदयग्रन्थेर्विनाशो यद्यशेषतः ।
अनिच्छोर्विषयः किं नु प्रवृत्तेः कारणं स्वतः ॥ ४२३ ॥
423.transliteration:
ajñānahṛdayagranthervināśo yadyaśeṣataḥ |
anicchorviṣayaḥ kiṃ nu pravṛtteḥ kāraṇaṃ svataḥ || 423 ||
423.translation: If the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed, what natural cause can there be for inducing such a man to selfish action, for he is averse to sense-pleasures?

424.shloka:
वासनानुदयो भोग्ये वैरागस्य तदावधिः ।
अहंभावोदयाभावो बोधस्य परमावधिः लीनवृत्तैरनुत्पत्तिर्मर्यादोपरतेस्तु सा ॥ ४२४ ॥
424.transliteration:
vāsanānudayo bhogye vairāgasya tadāvadhiḥ |
ahaṃbhāvodayābhāvo bodhasya paramāvadhiḥ līnavṛttairanutpattirmaryādoparatestu sā || 424 ||
424.translation: When the sense-objects excite no more desire, then is the culmination of dispassion. The extreme perfection of knowledge is the absence of any impulsion of the egoistic idea. And the limit of self-withdrawal is reached when the mind-functions that have been merged, appear no more.

425.shloka:
ब्रह्माकारतया सदा स्थिततया निर्मुक्तबाह्यार्थधीर् अन्यावेदितभोग्यभोगकलनो निद्रालुवद्बालवत् ।
स्वप्नालोकितलोकवज्जगदिदं पश्यन् क्वचिल्लब्धधीर् आस्ते कश्चिदनन्तपुण्यफलभुग्धन्यः स मान्यो भुवि ॥ ४२५ ॥
425.transliteration:
brahmākāratayā sadā sthitatayā nirmuktabāhyārthadhīr anyāveditabhogyabhogakalano nidrāluvadbālavat |
svapnālokitalokavajjagadidaṃ paśyan kvacillabdhadhīr āste kaścidanantapuṇyaphalabhugdhanyaḥ sa mānyo bhuvi || 425 ||
425.translation: Freed from all sense of reality of the external sense-objects on account of his always remaining merged in Brahman; only seeming to enjoy such sense-objects as are offered by others, like one sleepy, or like a child; beholding this world as one seen in dreams, and having cognition of it at chance moments – rare indeed is such a man, the enjoyer of the fruits of endless merit, and he alone is blessed and esteemed on earth.

426.shloka:
स्थितप्रज्ञो यतिरयं यः सदानन्दमश्नुते ।
ब्रह्मण्येव विलीनात्मा निर्विकारो विनिष्क्रियः ॥ ४२६ ॥
426.transliteration:
sthitaprajño yatirayaṃ yaḥ sadānandamaśnute |
brahmaṇyeva vilīnātmā nirvikāro viniṣkriyaḥ || 426 ||
426.translation: That Sannyasin has got a steady illumination who, having his soul wholly merged in Brahman, enjoys eternal bliss, is changeless and free from activity.

427.shloka:
ब्रह्मात्मनोः शोधितयोरेकभावावगाहिनी ।
निर्विकल्पा च चिन्मात्रा वृत्तिः प्रज्ञेति कथ्यते सुस्थितासौ भवेद्यस्य स्थितप्रज्ञः स उच्यते ॥ ४२७ ॥
427.transliteration:
brahmātmanoḥ śodhitayorekabhāvāvagāhinī |
nirvikalpā ca cinmātrā vṛttiḥ prajñeti kathyate susthitāsau bhavedyasya sthitaprajñaḥ sa ucyate || 427 ||
427.translation: That kind of mental function which cognises only the identity of the Self and Brahman, purified of all adjuncts, which is free from duality, and which concerns itself only with Pure Intelligence, is called illumination. He who has this perfectly steady is called a man of steady illumination.

428.shloka:
यस्य स्थिता भवेत्प्रज्ञा यस्यानन्दो निरन्तरः ।
प्रपञ्चो विस्मृतप्रायः स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४२८ ॥
428.transliteration:
yasya sthitā bhavetprajñā yasyānando nirantaraḥ |
prapañco vismṛtaprāyaḥ sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 428 ||
428.translation: He whose illumination is steady, who has constant bliss, and who has almost forgotten the phenomenal universe, is accepted as a man liberated in this very life.

429.shloka:
लीनधीरपि जागर्ति जाग्रद्धर्मविवर्जितः ।
बोधो निर्वासनो यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४२९ ॥
429.transliteration:
līnadhīrapi jāgarti jāgraddharmavivarjitaḥ |
bodho nirvāsano yasya sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 429 ||
429.translation: He who, even having his mind merged in Brahman, is nevertheless quite alert, but free at the same time from the characteristics of the waking state, and whose realisation is free from desires, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

430.shloka:
शान्तसंसारकलनः कलावानपि निष्कलः ।
यस्य चित्तं विनिश्चिन्तं स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४३0 ॥
430.transliteration:
śāntasaṃsārakalanaḥ kalāvānapi niṣkalaḥ |
yasya cittaṃ viniścintaṃ sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 430 ||
430.translation: He whose cares about the phenomenal state have been appeased, who, though possessed of a body consisting of parts, is yet devoid of parts, and whose mind is free from anxiety, is accepted as a man liberated-in-life.

431.translation: The absence of the ideas of 'I' and 'mine' even in this existing body which follows as a shadow, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

432.shloka:
अतीताननुसन्धानं भविष्यदविचारणम् ।
अउदासीन्यमपि प्राप्तं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३२ ॥
432.transliteration:
atītānanusandhānaṃ bhaviṣyadavicāraṇam |
audāsīnyamapi prāptaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 432 ||
432.translation: Not dwelling on enjoyments of the past, taking no thought for the future and looking with indifference upon the present, are characteristics of one liberated-in-life.

433.shloka:
गुणदोषविशिष्टेऽस्मिन्स्वभावेन विलक्षणे ।
सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं जीवन्मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४३३ ॥
433.transliteration:
guṇadoṣaviśiṣṭe'sminsvabhāvena vilakṣaṇe |
sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ jīvanmuktasya lakṣaṇam || 433 ||
433.translation: Looking everywhere with an eye of equality in this world, full of elements possessing merits and demerits, and distinct by nature from one another, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

434.translation: When things pleasant or painful present themselves, to remain unruffled in mind in both cases, through the sameness of attitude, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

435.translation: The absence of all ideas of interior or exterior in the case of a Sannyasin, owing to his mind being engrossed in tasting the bliss of Brahman, is a characteristic of one liberated-in-life.

436.shloka:
देहेन्द्रियादौ कर्तव्ये ममाहंभाववर्जितः ।
अउदासीन्येन यस्तिष्ठेत्स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३६ ॥
436.transliteration:
dehendriyādau kartavye mamāhaṃbhāvavarjitaḥ |
audāsīnyena yastiṣṭhetsa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 436 ||
436.translation: He who lives unconcerned, devoid of all ideas of 'I' and 'mine' with regard to the body, organs, etc., as well as to his duties, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

437.shloka:
विज्ञात आत्मनो यस्य ब्रह्मभावः श्रुतेर्बलात् ।
भवबन्धविनिर्मुक्तः स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३७ ॥
437.transliteration:
vijñāta ātmano yasya brahmabhāvaḥ śruterbalāt |
bhavabandhavinirmuktaḥ sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 437 ||
437.translation: He who has realised his Brahmanhood aided by the Scriptures, and is free from the bondage of transmigration, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

438.shloka:
देहेन्द्रियेष्वहंभाव इदंभावस्तदन्यके ।
यस्य नो भवतः क्वापि स जीवन्मुक्त इष्यते ॥ ४३८ ॥
438.transliteration:
dehendriyeṣvahaṃbhāva idaṃbhāvastadanyake |
yasya no bhavataḥ kvāpi sa jīvanmukta iṣyate || 438 ||
438.translation: He who never has the idea of 'I' with regard to the body, organs, etc., nor that of 'it' in respect of things other than these, is accepted as one liberated-in-life.

439.shloka:
न प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मणोर्भेदं कदापि ब्रह्मसर्गयोः ।
प्रज्ञया यो विजानिति स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४३९ ॥
439.transliteration:
na pratyagbrahmaṇorbhedaṃ kadāpi brahmasargayoḥ |
prajñayā yo vijāniti sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 439 ||
439.translation: He who through his illumination never differentiates the Jiva and Brahman, nor the universe and Brahman, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

440.shloka:
साधुभिः पूज्यमानेऽस्मिन् पीड्यमानेऽपि दुर्जनैः ।
समभावो भवेद्यस्य स जीवन्मुक्तलक्षणः ॥ ४४0 ॥
440.transliteration:
sādhubhiḥ pūjyamāne'smin pīḍyamāne'pi durjanaiḥ |
samabhāvo bhavedyasya sa jīvanmuktalakṣaṇaḥ || 440 ||
440.translation: He who feels just the same when his body is either worshipped by the good or tormented by the wicked, is known as a man liberated-in-life.

441.shloka:
यत्र प्रविष्टा विषयाः परेरिता नदीप्रवाहा इव वारिराशौ ।
लिनन्ति सन्मात्रतया न विक्रियां उत्पादयन्त्येष यतिर्विमुक्तः ॥ ४४१ ॥
441.transliteration:
yatra praviṣṭā viṣayāḥ pareritā nadīpravāhā iva vārirāśau |
linanti sanmātratayā na vikriyāṃ utpādayantyeṣa yatirvimuktaḥ || 441 ||
441.translation: The Sannyasin in whom the sense-objects directed by others are engulfed like flowing rivers in the sea and produce no change, owing to his identity with the Existence Absolute, is indeed liberated.

442.shloka:
विज्ञातब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य यथापूर्वं न संसृतिः ।
अस्ति चेन्न स विज्ञातब्रह्मभावो बहिर्मुखः ॥ ४४२ ॥
442.transliteration:
vijñātabrahmatattvasya yathāpūrvaṃ na saṃsṛtiḥ |
asti cenna sa vijñātabrahmabhāvo bahirmukhaḥ || 442 ||
442.translation: For one who has realised the Truth of Brahman, there is no more attachment to the sense-objects as before: If there is, that man has not realised his identity with Brahman, but is one whose senses are outgoing in their tendency.

443.shloka:
प्राचीनवासनावेगादसौ संसरतीति चेत् ।
न सदेकत्वविज्ञानान्मन्दी भवति वासना ॥ ४४३ ॥
443.transliteration:
prācīnavāsanāvegādasau saṃsaratīti cet |
na sadekatvavijñānānmandī bhavati vāsanā || 443 ||
443.translation: If it be urged that he is still attached to the sense-objects through the momentum of his old desires, the reply is – no, for desires get weakened through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman.

444.shloka:
अत्यन्तकामुकस्यापि वृत्तिः कुण्ठति मातरि ।
तथैव ब्रह्मणि ज्ञाते पूर्णानन्दे मनीषिणः ॥ ४४४ ॥
444.transliteration:
atyantakāmukasyāpi vṛttiḥ kuṇṭhati mātari |
tathaiva brahmaṇi jñāte pūrṇānande manīṣiṇaḥ || 444 ||
444.translation: The propensities of even a confirmed libertine are checked in the presence of his mother; just so, when Brahman, the Bliss Absolute, has been realised, the man of realisation has no longer any worldly tendency.

445.shloka:
निदिध्यासनशीलस्य बाह्यप्रत्यय ईक्ष्यते ।
ब्रवीति श्रुतिरेतस्य प्रारब्धं फलदर्शनात् ॥ ४४५ ॥
445.transliteration:
nididhyāsanaśīlasya bāhyapratyaya īkṣyate |
bravīti śrutiretasya prārabdhaṃ phaladarśanāt || 445 ||
445.translation: One who is constantly practising meditation is observed to have external perceptions. The Śrutis mention Prārabdha work in the case of such a man, and we can infer this from results actually seen.

446.shloka:
सुखाद्यनुभवो यावत्तावत्प्रारब्धमिष्यते ।
फलोदयः क्रियापूर्वो निष्क्रियो न हि कुत्रचित् ॥ ४४६ ॥
446.transliteration:
sukhādyanubhavo yāvattāvatprārabdhamiṣyate |
phalodayaḥ kriyāpūrvo niṣkriyo na hi kutracit || 446 ||
446.translation: Prārabdha work is acknowledged to persist so long as there is the perception of happiness and the like. Every result is preceded by an action, and nowhere is it seen to accrue independently of action.

447.shloka:
अहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानात्कल्पकोटिशतार्जितम् ।
सञ्चितं विलयं याति प्रबोधात्स्वप्नकर्मवत् ॥ ४४७ ॥
447.transliteration:
ahaṃ brahmeti vijñānātkalpakoṭiśatārjitam |
sañcitaṃ vilayaṃ yāti prabodhātsvapnakarmavat || 447 ||
447.translation: Through the realisation of one’s identity with Brahman, all the accumulated actions of a hundred crore of cycles come to nought, like the actions of dream-state on awakening.

448.shloka:
यत्कृतं स्वप्नवेलायां पुण्यं वा पापमुल्बणम् ।
सुप्तोत्थितस्य किं तत्स्यात्स्वर्गाय नरकाय वा ॥ ४४८ ॥
448.transliteration:
yatkṛtaṃ svapnavelāyāṃ puṇyaṃ vā pāpamulbaṇam |
suptotthitasya kiṃ tatsyātsvargāya narakāya vā || 448 ||
448.translation: Can the good actions or dreadful sins that a man fancies himself doing in the dream-state, lead him to heaven or hell after he has awakened from sleep?

449.shloka:
स्वमसङ्गमुदासीनं परिज्ञाय नभो यथा ।
न श्लिष्यति च यत्किंचित्कदाचिद्भाविकर्मभिः ॥ ४४९ ॥
449.transliteration:
svamasaṅgamudāsīnaṃ parijñāya nabho yathā |
na śliṣyati ca yatkiṃcitkadācidbhāvikarmabhiḥ || 449 ||
449.translation: Realising the Ātman, which is unattached and indifferent like the sky, the aspirant is never touched in the least by actions yet to be done.

450.shloka:
न नभो घटयोगेन सुरागन्धेन लिप्यते ।
तथात्मोपाधियोगेन तद्धर्मैर्नैव लिप्यते ॥ ४५0 ॥
450.transliteration:
na nabho ghaṭayogena surāgandhena lipyate |
tathātmopādhiyogena taddharmairnaiva lipyate || 450 ||
450.translation: The sky is not affected by the smell of liquor merely through its connection with the jar; similarly, the Ātman is not, through Its connection with the limitations, affected by the properties thereof.

451.shloka:
ज्ञानोदयात्पुरारब्धं कर्मज्ञानान्न नश्यति ।
अदत्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् ॥ ४५१ ॥
451.transliteration:
jñānodayātpurārabdhaṃ karmajñānānna naśyati |
adatvā svaphalaṃ lakṣyamuddiśyotsṛṣṭabāṇavat || 451 ||
451.translation: The work which has fashioned this body prior to the dawning of knowledge, is not destroyed by that knowledge without yielding its fruits, like the arrow shot at an object.

452.shloka:
व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ ।
न तिष्ठति छिनत्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥ ४५२ ॥
452.transliteration:
vyāghrabuddhyā vinirmukto bāṇaḥ paścāttu gomatau |
na tiṣṭhati chinatyeva lakṣyaṃ vegena nirbharam || 452 ||
452.translation: The arrow which is shot at an object with the idea that it is a tiger, does not, when that object is perceived to be a cow, check itself, but pierces the object with full force.

453.shloka:
प्राब्धं बलवत्तरं खलु विदां भोगेन तस्य क्षयः सम्यग्ज्ञानहुताशनेन विलयः प्राक्षंचितागामिनाम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमवेक्ष्य तन्मायातया ये सर्वदा संस्थिताः तेषां तत्त्रितयं नहि क्वचिदपि ब्रह्मैव ते निर्गुणम् ॥ ४५३ ॥
453.transliteration:
prābdhaṃ balavattaraṃ khalu vidāṃ bhogena tasya kṣayaḥ samyagjñānahutāśanena vilayaḥ prākṣaṃcitāgāminām |
brahmātmaikyamavekṣya tanMāyātayā ye sarvadā saṃsthitāḥ teṣāṃ tattritayaṃ nahi kvacidapi brahmaiva te nirguṇam || 453 ||
453.translation: Prārabdha work is certainly very strong for the man of realisation, and is spent only by the actual experience of its fruit; while the actions previously accumulated and those yet to come are destroyed by the fire of perfect knowledge. But none of the three at all affects those who, realising their identity with Brahman, are always living absorbed in that idea. They are verily the transcendent Brahman.

454.shloka:
उपाधितादात्म्यविहीनकेवल ब्रह्मात्मनैवात्मनि तिष्ठतो मुनेः ।
प्रारब्धसद्भावकथा न युक्ता स्वप्नार्थसंबन्धकथेव जाग्रतः ॥ ४५४ ॥
454.transliteration:
upādhitādātmyavihīnakevala brahmātmanaivātmani tiṣṭhato muneḥ |
prārabdhasadbhāvakathā na yuktā svapnārthasaṃbandhakatheva jāgrataḥ || 454 ||
454.translation: For the sage who lives in his own Self as Brahman, the One without a second, devoid of identification with the limiting adjuncts, the question of the existence of Prārabdha work is meaningless, like the question of a man who has awakened from sleep having any connection with the objects seen in the dream-state.

455.shloka:
न हि प्रबुद्धः प्रतिभासदेहे देहोपयोगिन्यपि च प्रपञ्चे ।
करोत्यहन्तां ममतानिदन्तां किन्तु स्वयं तिष्ठति जागरेण ॥ ४५५ ॥
455.transliteration:
na hi prabuddhaḥ pratibhāsadehe dehopayoginyapi ca prapañce |
karotyahantāṃ mamatānidantāṃ kintu svayaṃ tiṣṭhati jāgareṇa || 455 ||
455.translation: The man who has awakened from sleep never has any idea of 'I' or 'mine' with regard to his dream-body and the dream-objects that ministered to that body, but lives quite awake, as his own Self.

456.shloka:
न तस्य मिथ्यार्थसमर्थनेच्छा न संग्रहस्तज्जगतोऽपि दृष्टः ।
तत्रानुवृत्तिर्यदि चेन्मृषार्थे न निद्रया मुक्त इतीष्यते ध्रुवम् ॥ ४५६ ॥
456.transliteration:
na tasya mithyārthasamarthanecchā na saṃgrahastajjagato'pi dṛṣṭaḥ |
tatrānuvṛttiryadi cenmṛṣārthe na nidrayā mukta itīṣyate dhruvam || 456 ||
456.translation: He has no desire to substantiate the unreal objects, nor is he seen to maintain that dream-world. If he still clings to those unreal objects, he is emphatically declared to be not yet free from sleep.

457.shloka:
तद्वत्परे ब्रह्मणि वर्तमानः सदात्मना तिष्ठति नान्यदीक्षते ।
स्मृतिर्यथा स्वप्नविलोकितार्थे तथा विदः प्राशनमोचनादौ ॥ ४५७ ॥
457.transliteration:
tadvatpare brahmaṇi vartamānaḥ sadātmanā tiṣṭhati nānyadīkṣate |
smṛtiryathā svapnavilokitārthe tathā vidaḥ prāśanamocanādau || 457 ||
457.translation: Similarly, he who is absorbed in Brahman lives identified with that eternal Reality and beholds nothing else. As one has a memory of the objects seen in a dream, so the man of realisation has a memory of the everyday actions such as eating.

458.shloka:
कर्मणा निर्मितो देहः प्रारब्धं तस्य कल्प्यताम् ।
नानादेरात्मनो युक्तं नैवात्मा कर्मनिर्मितः ॥ ४५८ ॥
458.transliteration:
karmaṇā nirmito dehaḥ prārabdhaṃ tasya kalpyatām |
nānāderātmano yuktaṃ naivātmā karmanirmitaḥ || 458 ||
458.translation: The body has been fashioned by Karma, so one may imagine Prarabdha work with reference to it. But it is not reasonable to attribute the same to the Ātman, for the Ātman is never the outcome of work.

459.shloka:
अजो नित्यः शाश्वत इति ब्रूते श्रुतिरमोघवाक् ।
तदात्मना तिष्ठतोऽस्य कुतः प्रारब्धकल्पना ॥ ४५९ ॥
459.transliteration:
ajo nityaḥ śāśvata iti brūte śrutiramoghavāk |
tadātmanā tiṣṭhato'sya kutaḥ prārabdhakalpanā || 459 ||
459.translation: The Śrutis, whose words are infallible, declare the Ātman to be 'birthless, eternal and undecaying'. So, the man who lives identified with That, how can Prārabdha work be attributed?

460.shloka:
प्रारब्धं सिध्यति तदा यदा देहात्मना स्थितिः ।
देहात्मभावो नैवेष्टः प्रारब्धं त्यज्यतामतः ॥ ४६0 ॥
460.transliteration:
prārabdhaṃ sidhyati tadā yadā dehātmanā sthitiḥ |
dehātmabhāvo naiveṣṭaḥ prārabdhaṃ tyajyatāmataḥ || 460 ||
460.translation: Prārabdha work can be maintained only so long as one lives identified with the body. But no one admits that the man of realisation ever identifies himself with the body. Hence Prārabdha work should be rejected in his case.

461.shloka:
शरीरस्यापि प्रारब्धकल्पना भ्रान्तिरेव हि ।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतः सत्त्वमसत्यस्य कुतो जनिः अजातस्य कुतो नाशः प्रारब्धमसतः कुतः ॥ ४६१ ॥
461.transliteration:
śarīrasyāpi prārabdhakalpanā bhrāntireva hi |
adhyastasya kutaḥ sattvamasatyasya kuto janiḥ ajātasya kuto nāśaḥ prārabdhamasataḥ kutaḥ || 461 ||
461.translation: The attributing of Prārabdha work to the body even is certainly an error. How can something that is superimposed (on another) have any existence, and how can that which is unreal have a birth? And how can that which has not been born at all, die? So how can Prārabdha work exist for something that is unreal?

462.shloka:
ज्ञानेनाज्ञानकार्यस्य समूलस्य लयो यदि ।
तिष्ठत्ययं कथं देह इति शङ्कावतो जडान् ॥ ४६२ ॥ समाधातुं बाह्यदृष्ट्या प्रारब्धं वदति श्रुतिः ।
न तु देहादिसत्यत्वबोधनाय विपश्चिताम् ॥ ४६३ ॥
462.transliteration:
jñānenājñānakāryasya samūlasya layo yadi |
tiṣṭhatyayaṃ kathaṃ deha iti śaṅkāvato jaḍān || 462 || samādhātuṃ bāhyadṛṣṭyā prārabdhaṃ vadati śrutiḥ |
na tu dehādisatyatvabodhanāya vipaścitām || 463 ||
462.translation: 462-463. 'If the effects of ignorance are destroyed with their root by knowledge, then how does the body live?' – it is to convince those fools who entertain a doubt like this, that the Śrutis, from a relative standpoint, hypothesise Prārabdha work, but not for proving the reality of the body etc., of the man of realisation.

463.shloka:
परिपूर्णमनाद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६४ ॥
463.transliteration:
paripūrṇamanādyantamaprameyamavikriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 464 ||
463.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

464.shloka:
परिपूर्णमनाद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६४ ॥
464.transliteration:
paripūrṇamanādyantamaprameyamavikriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 464 ||
464.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

465.shloka:
सद्गनं चिद्घनं नित्यमानन्दघनमक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६५ ॥
465.transliteration:
sadganaṃ cidghanaṃ nityamānandaghanamakriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 465 ||
465.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Essence of Existence, Knowledge and Eternal Bliss, and devoid of activity; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

466.shloka:
प्रत्यगेकरसं पूर्णमनन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६६ ॥
466.transliteration:
pratyagekarasaṃ pūrṇamanantaṃ sarvatomukham |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 466 ||
466.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is within all, homogeneous, infinite, endless, and all-pervading; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

467.shloka:
अहेयमनुपादेयमनादेयमनाश्रयम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६७ ॥
467.transliteration:
aheyamanupādeyamanādeyamanāśrayam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 467 ||
467.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is neither to be shunned nor taken up nor accepted, and which is without any support, there is no duality whatsoever in It.

468.shloka:
निर्गुणं निष्कलं सूक्ष्मं निर्विकल्पं निरञ्जनम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६८ ॥
468.transliteration:
nirguṇaṃ niṣkalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nirvikalpaṃ nirañjanam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 468 ||
468.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, beyond attributes, without parts, subtle, absolute and taintless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

469.shloka:
अनिरूप्य स्वरूपं यन्मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६९ ॥
469.transliteration:
anirūpya svarūpaṃ yanmanovācāmagocaram |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 469 ||
469.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, whose real nature is incomprehensible, and which is beyond the range of mind and speech; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

470.shloka:
सत्समृद्धं स्वतःसिद्धं शुद्धं बुद्धमनीदृशम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४७0 ॥
470.transliteration:
satsamṛddhaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ śuddhaṃ buddhamanīdṛśam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 470 ||
470.translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Reality, the One without a second, the Reality, effulgent, self-existent, pure, intelligent, and unlike anything finite; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

471.shloka:
निरस्तरागा विनिरस्तभोगाः शान्ताः सुदान्ता यतयो महान्तः ।
विज्ञाय तत्त्वं परमेतदन्ते प्राप्ताः परां निर्वृतिमात्मयोगात् ॥ ४७१ ॥
471.transliteration:
nirastarāgā vinirastabhogāḥ śāntāḥ sudāntā yatayo mahāntaḥ |
vijñāya tattvaṃ parametadante prāptāḥ parāṃ nirvṛtimātmayogāt || 471 ||
471.translation: High-souled Sannyasins who have got rid of all attachment and discarded all sense- enjoyments, and who are serene and perfectly restrained, realise this Supreme Truth and at the end attain the Supreme Bliss through their Self-realisation.

472.shloka:
भवानपीदं परतत्त्वमात्मनः स्वरूपमानन्दघनं विचार्य ।
विधूय मोहं स्वमनःप्रकल्पितं मुक्तः कृतार्थो भवतु प्रबुद्धः ॥ ४७२ ॥
472.transliteration:
bhavānapīdaṃ paratattvamātmanaḥ svarūpamānandaghanaṃ vicārya |
vidhūya mohaṃ svamanaḥprakalpitaṃ muktaḥ kṛtārtho bhavatu prabuddhaḥ || 472 ||
472.translation: Thou, too, discriminate this Supreme Truth, the real nature of the Self, which is Bliss undiluted, and shaking off thy delusion created by thy own mind, be free and illumined, and attain the consummation of thy life.

473.shloka:
समाधिना साधुविनिश्चलात्मना पश्यात्मतत्त्वं स्फुटबोधचक्षुषा ।
निःसंशयं सम्यगवेक्षितश्चेच् छ्रुतः पदार्थो न पुनर्विकल्प्यते ॥ ४७३ ॥
473.transliteration:
samādhinā sādhuviniścalātmanā paśyātmatattvaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā |
niḥsaṃśayaṃ samyagavekṣitaścec chrutaḥ padārtho na punarvikalpyate || 473 ||
473.translation: Through the Samadhi in which the mind has been perfectly stilled, visualise the Truth of the Self with the eye of clear realisation. If the meaning of the (Scriptural) words heard from the Guru is perfectly and indubitably discerned, then it can lead to no more doubt.

474.shloka:
स्वस्याविद्याबन्धसंबन्धमोक्षात् सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपात्मलब्धौ ।
शास्त्रं युक्तिर्देशिकोक्तिः प्रमाणं चान्तःसिद्धा स्वानुभूतिः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७४ ॥
474.transliteration:
svasyāvidyābandhasaṃbandhamokṣāt satyajñānānandarūpātmalabdhau |
śāstraṃ yuktirdeśikoktiḥ pramāṇaṃ cāntaḥsiddhā svānubhūtiḥ pramāṇam || 474 ||
474.translation: In the realisation of the Ātman, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, through the breaking of one’s connection with the bondage of Avidya or ignorance, the Scriptures, reasoning and the words of the Guru are the proofs, while one’s own experience earned by concentrating the mind is another proof.

475.shloka:
बन्धो मोक्षश्च तृप्तिश्च चिन्तारोग्यक्षुदादयः ।
स्वेनैव वेद्या यज्ज्ञानं परेषामानुमानिकम् ॥ ४७५ ॥
475.transliteration:
bandho mokṣaśca tṛptiśca cintārogyakṣudādayaḥ |
svenaiva vedyā yajjñānaṃ pareṣāmānumānikam || 475 ||
475.translation: Bondage, liberation, satisfaction, anxiety, recovery from illness, hunger and other such things are known only to the man concerned, and knowledge of these to others is a mere inference.

476.shloka:
तटस्थिता बोधयन्ति गुरवः श्रुतयो यथा ।
प्रज्ञयैव तरेद्विद्वानीश्वरानुगृहीतया ॥ ४७६ ॥
476.transliteration:
taṭasthitā bodhayanti guravaḥ śrutayo yathā |
prajñayaiva taredvidvānīśvarānugṛhītayā || 476 ||
476.translation: The Gurus as well as the Śrutis instruct the disciple, standing aloof; while the man of realisation crosses (Avidya) through Illumination alone, backed by the grace of God.

477.shloka:
स्वानुभूत्या स्वयं ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डितम् ।
संसिद्धः संमुखं तिष्ठेन्निर्विकल्पात्मनात्मनि ॥ ४७७ ॥
477.transliteration:
svānubhūtyā svayaṃ jñātvā svamātmānamakhaṇḍitam |
saṃsiddhaḥ saṃmukhaṃ tiṣṭhennirvikalpātmanātmani || 477 ||
477.translation: Himself knowing his indivisible Self through his own realisation and thus becoming perfect, a man should stand face to face with the Ātman, with his mind free from dualistic ideas.

478.shloka:
वेदान्तसिद्धान्तनिरुक्तिरेषा ब्रह्मैव जीवः सकलं जगच्च ।
अखण्डरूपस्थितिरेव मोक्षो ब्रह्माद्वितीये श्रुतयः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७८ ॥
478.transliteration:
vedāntasiddhāntaniruktireṣā brahmaiva jīvaḥ sakalaṃ jagacca |
akhaṇḍarūpasthitireva mokṣo brahmādvitīye śrutayaḥ pramāṇam || 478 ||
478.translation: The verdict of all discussions on the Vedanta is that the Jīva and the whole universe are nothing but Brahman, and that liberation means abiding in Brahman, the indivisible Entity. While the Śrutis themselves are authority (for the statement) that Brahman is One without a second.

479.shloka:
