इति गुरुवचनाच्छ्रुतिप्रमाणात् परमवगम्य सतत्त्वमात्मयुक्त्या ।
प्रशमितकरणः समाहितात्मा क्वचिदचलाकृतिरात्मनिष्ठतोऽभूत् ॥ ४७९ ॥
479.transliteration:
iti guruvacanācchrutipramāṇāt paramavagamya satattvamātmayuktyā |
praśamitakaraṇaḥ samāhitātmā kvacidacalākṛtirātmaniṣṭhato'bhūt || 479 ||
479.translation: Realising, at a blessed moment, the Supreme Truth through the above instructions of the Guru, the authority of the Scriptures and his own reasoning, with his senses quieted and the mind concentrated, (the disciple) became immovable in form and perfectly established in the Ātman.

480.shloka:
किंचित्कालं समाधाय परे ब्रह्मणि मानसम् ।
उत्थाय परमानन्दादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ ४८0 ॥
480.transliteration:
kiṃcitkālaṃ samādhāya pare brahmaṇi mānasam |
utthāya paramānandādidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 480 ||
480.translation: Concentrating the mind for some time on the Supreme Brahman, he rose, and out of supreme bliss spoke as follows.

481.shloka:
बुद्धिर्विनष्टा गलिता प्रवृत्तिः ब्रह्मात्मनोरेकतयाधिगत्या ।
इदं न जानेऽप्यनिदं न जाने किं वा कियद्वा सुखमस्त्यपारम् ॥ ४८१ ॥
481.transliteration:
buddhirvinaṣṭā galitā pravṛttiḥ brahmātmanorekatayādhigatyā |
idaṃ na jāne'pyanidaṃ na jāne kiṃ vā kiyadvā sukhamastyapāram || 481 ||
481.translation: My mind has vanished, and all its activities have melted, by realising the identity of the Self and Brahman; I do not know either this or not-this; nor what or how much the boundless Bliss (of Samadhi) is!

482.shloka:
वाचा वक्तुमशक्यमेव मनसा मन्तुं न वा शक्यते स्वानन्दामृतपूरपूरितपरब्रह्माम्बुधेर्वैभवम् ।
अम्भोराशिविशीर्णवार्षिकशिलाभावं भजन्मे मनो यस्यांशांशलवे विलीनमधुनानन्दात्मना निर्वृतम् ॥ ४८२ ॥
482.transliteration:
vācā vaktumaśakyameva manasā mantuṃ na vā śakyate svānandāmṛtapūrapūritaparabrahmāmbudhervaibhavam |
ambhorāśiviśīrṇavārṣikaśilābhāvaṃ bhajanme mano yasyāṃśāṃśalave vilīnamadhunānandātmanā nirvṛtam || 482 ||
482.translation: The majesty of the ocean of Supreme Brahman, replete with the swell of the nectar-like Bliss of the Self, is verily impossible to express in speech, nor can it be conceived by the mind – in an infinitesimal fraction of which my mind melted like a hailstone getting merged in the ocean, and is now satisfied with that Essence of Bliss.

483.shloka:
क्व गतं केन वा नीतं कुत्र लीनमिदं जगत् ।
अधुनैव मया दृष्टं नास्ति किं महदद्भुतम् ॥ ४८३ ॥
483.transliteration:
kva gataṃ kena vā nītaṃ kutra līnamidaṃ jagat |
adhunaiva mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nāsti kiṃ mahadadbhutam || 483 ||
483.translation: Where is the universe gone, by whom is it removed, and where is it merged? It was just now seen by me, and has it ceased to exist? It is passing strange!

484.shloka:
किं हेयं किमुपादेयं किमन्यत्किं विलक्षणम् ।
अखण्डानन्दपीयूषपूर्णे ब्रह्ममहार्णवे ॥ ४८४ ॥
484.transliteration:
kiṃ heyaṃ kimupādeyaṃ kimanyatkiṃ vilakṣaṇam |
akhaṇḍānandapīyūṣapūrṇe brahmamahārṇave || 484 ||
484.translation: In the ocean of Brahman filled with the nectar of Absolute Bliss, what is to be shunned and what accepted, what is other (than oneself) and what different?

485.shloka:
न किंचिदत्र पश्यामि न शृणोमि न वेद्म्यहम् ।
स्वात्मनैव सदानन्दरूपेणास्मि विलक्षणः ॥ ४८५ ॥
485.transliteration:
na kiṃcidatra paśyāmi na śṛṇomi na vedmyaham |
svātmanaiva sadānandarūpeṇāsmi vilakṣaṇaḥ || 485 ||
485.translation: I neither see nor hear nor know anything in this. I simply exist as the Self, the eternal Bliss, distinct from everything else.

486.shloka:
नमो नमस्ते गुरवे महात्मने विमुक्तसङ्गाय सदुत्तमाय ।
नित्याद्वयानन्दरसस्वरूपिणे भूम्ने सदापारदयाम्बुधाम्ने ॥ ४८६ ॥
486.transliteration:
namo namaste gurave mahātmane vimuktasaṅgāya saduttamāya |
nityādvayānandarasasvarūpiṇe bhūmne sadāpāradayāmbudhāmne || 486 ||
486.translation: Repeated salutations to thee, O noble Teacher, who art devoid of attachment, the best among the good souls and the embodiment of the essence of Eternal Bliss, the One without a second – who art infinite and ever the boundless ocean of mercy:

487.translation: Whose glance, like the shower of concentrated moonbeams, has removed my exhaustion brought on by the afflictions of the world, and in a moment admitted me to the undecaying status of the Ātman, the Bliss of infinite majesty!

488.shloka:
धन्योऽहं कृतकृत्योऽहं विमुक्तोऽहं भवग्रहात् ।
नित्यानन्दस्वरूपोऽहं पूर्णोऽहं त्वदनुग्रहात् ॥ ४८८ ॥
488.transliteration:
dhanyo'haṃ kṛtakṛtyo'haṃ vimukto'haṃ bhavagrahāt |
nityānandasvarūpo'haṃ pūrṇo'haṃ tvadanugrahāt || 488 ||
488.translation: Blessed am I; I have attained the consummation of my life, and am free from the clutches of transmigration; I am the Essence of Eternal Bliss, I am infinite – all through thy mercy!

489.translation: I am unattached, I am disembodied, I am free from the subtle body, and undecaying, I am serene, I am infinite, I am taintless and eternal.

490.translation: I am not the doer, I am not the experiencer, I am changeless and beyond activity; I am the essence of Pure Knowledge; I am Absolute and identified with Eternal Good.

491.translation: I am indeed different from the seer, listener, speaker, doer and experiencer; I am the essence of Knowledge, eternal, without any break, beyond activity, limitless, unattached and infinite.

492.shloka:
नाहमिदं नाहमदोऽप्युभयोरवभासकं परं शुद्धम् ।
बाह्याभ्यन्तरशून्यं पूर्णं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९२ ॥
492.transliteration:
nāhamidaṃ nāhamado'pyubhayoravabhāsakaṃ paraṃ śuddham |
bāhyābhyantaraśūnyaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 492 ||
492.translation: I am neither, this nor that, but the Supreme, the illuminer of both; I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, pure, devoid of interior or exterior and infinite.

493.shloka:
निरुपममनादितत्त्वं त्वमहमिदमद इति कल्पनादूरम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं सत्यं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९३ ॥
493.transliteration:
nirupamamanāditattvaṃ tvamahamidamada iti kalpanādūram |
nityānandaikarasaṃ satyaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 493 ||
493.translation: I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, matchless, the Reality that has no beginning, beyond such imagination as thou or I, or this or that, the Essence of Eternal Bliss, the Truth.

494.shloka:
नारायणोऽहं नरकान्तकोऽहं पुरान्तकोऽहं पुरुषोऽहमीशः ।
अखण्डबोधोऽहमशेषसाक्षी निरीश्वरोऽहं निरहं च निर्ममः ॥ ४९४ ॥
494.transliteration:
nārāyaṇo'haṃ narakāntako'haṃ purāntako'haṃ puruṣo'hamīśaḥ |
akhaṇḍabodho'hamaśeṣasākṣī nirīśvaro'haṃ nirahaṃ ca nirmamaḥ || 494 ||
494.translation: I am Nārāyaṇa, the slayer of Nāraka; I am the destroyer of Tripura, the Supreme Being, the Ruler; I am knowledge Absolute, the Witness of everything; I have no other Ruler but myself, I am devoid of the ideas of 'I’ and 'mine'.

495.shloka:
सर्वेषु भूतेष्वहमेव संस्थितो ज्ञानात्मनान्तर्बहिराश्रयः सन् ।
भोक्ता च भोग्यं स्वयमेव सर्वं यद्यत्पृथग्दृष्टमिदन्तया पुरा ॥ ४९५ ॥
495.transliteration:
sarveṣu bhūteṣvahameva saṃsthito jñānātmanāntarbahirāśrayaḥ san |
bhoktā ca bhogyaṃ svayameva sarvaṃ yadyatpṛthagdṛṣṭamidantayā purā || 495 ||
495.translation: I alone reside as knowledge in all beings, being their internal and external support. I myself am the experiencer and all that is experienced – whatever I looked upon as 'this' or the not-Self previously.

496.shloka:
मय्यखण्डसुखाम्भोधौ बहुधा विश्ववीचयः ।
उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते मायामारुतविभ्रमात् ॥ ४९६ ॥
496.transliteration:
mayyakhaṇḍasukhāmbhodhau bahudhā viśvavīcayaḥ |
utpadyante vilīyante māyāmārutavibhramāt || 496 ||
496.translation: In me, the ocean of Infinite Bliss, the waves of the universe are created and destroyed by the playing of the wind of Māyā.

497.shloka:
स्थुलादिभावा मयि कल्पिता भ्रमाद् आरोपितानुस्फुरणेन लोकैः ।
काले यथा कल्पकवत्सराय णर्त्वादयो निष्कलनिर्विकल्पे ॥ ४९७ ॥
497.transliteration:
sthulādibhāvā mayi kalpitā bhramād āropitānusphuraṇena lokaiḥ |
kāle yathā kalpakavatsarāya ṇartvādayo niṣkalanirvikalpe || 497 ||
497.translation: Such ideas as gross (or subtle) are erroneously imagined in me by people through the manifestation of things superimposed – just as in the indivisible and absolute time, cycles, years, half-years, seasons, etc., are imagined.

498.shloka:
आरोपितं नाश्रयदूषकं भवेत् कदापि मूढैरतिदोषदूषितैः ।
नार्द्रिकरोत्यूषरभूमिभागं मरीचिकावारि महाप्रवाहः ॥ ४९८ ॥
498.transliteration:
āropitaṃ nāśrayadūṣakaṃ bhavet kadāpi mūḍhairatidoṣadūṣitaiḥ |
nārdrikarotyūṣarabhūmibhāgaṃ marīcikāvāri mahāpravāhaḥ || 498 ||
498.translation: That which is superimposed by the grossly ignorant fools can never taint the substratum: The great rush of waters observed in a mirage never wets the desert tracts.

499.translation: I am beyond contamination like the sky; I am distinct from things illumined, like the sun; I am always motionless like the mountain; I am limitless like the ocean.

500.shloka:
न मे देहेन संबन्धो मेघेनेव विहायसः ।
अतः कुतो मे तद्धर्मा जाक्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तयः ॥ ५00 ॥
500.transliteration:
na me dehena saṃbandho megheneva vihāyasaḥ |
ataḥ kuto me taddharmā jākratsvapnasuṣuptayaḥ || 500 ||
500.translation: I have no connection with the body, as the sky with clouds; so how can the states of wakefulness, dream and profound sleep, which are attributes of the body, affect me?

501.shloka:
उपाधिरायाति स एव गच्छति स एव कर्माणि करोति भुङ्क्ते ।
स एव जीर्यन्म्रियते सदाहं कुलाद्रिवन्निश्चल एव संस्थितः ॥ ५0१ ॥
501.transliteration:
upādhirāyāti sa eva gacchati sa eva karmāṇi karoti bhuṅkte |
sa eva jīryanmriyate sadāhaṃ kulādrivanniścala eva saṃsthitaḥ || 501 ||
501.translation: It is the Upādhi (superimposed attribute) that comes, and it is that alone which goes; that, again, performs actions and experiences (their fruits), that alone decays and dies, whereas I ever remain firm like the Kula mountain.

502.shloka:
न मे प्रवृत्तिर्न च मे निवृत्तिः सदैकरूपस्य निरंशकस्य ।
एकात्मको यो निविडो निरन्तरो व्योमेव पूर्णः स कथं नु चेष्टते ॥ ५0२ ॥
502.transliteration:
na me pravṛttirna ca me nivṛttiḥ sadaikarūpasya niraṃśakasya |
ekātmako yo niviḍo nirantaro vyomeva pūrṇaḥ sa kathaṃ nu ceṣṭate || 502 ||
502.translation: There is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it, for me who am always the same and devoid of parts, there is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it. How can that which is One, concentrated, without break and infinite like the sky, ever exert?

503.shloka:
पुण्यानि पापानि निरिन्द्रियस्य निश्चेतसो निर्विकृतेर्निराकृतेः ।
कुतो ममाखण्डसुखानुभूतेः ब्रूते ह्यनन्वागतमित्यपि श्रुतिः ॥ ५0३ ॥
503.transliteration:
puṇyāni pāpāni nirindriyasya niścetaso nirvikṛternirākṛteḥ |
kuto mamākhaṇḍasukhānubhūteḥ brūte hyananvāgatamityapi śrutiḥ || 503 ||
503.translation: How can there be merits and demerits for me, who am without organs, without mind, changeless, and formless – who am the realisation of Bliss Absolute? The Shruti also mentions this in the passage 'Not touched', etc.

504.shloka:
छायया स्पृष्टमुष्णं वा शीतं वा सुष्ठु दुःष्ठु वा ।
न स्पृशत्येव यत्किंचित्पुरुषं तद्विलक्षणम् ॥ ५0४ ॥
504.transliteration:
chāyayā spṛṣṭamuṣṇaṃ vā śītaṃ vā suṣṭhu duḥṣṭhu vā |
na spṛśatyeva yatkiṃcitpuruṣaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam || 504 ||
504.translation: If heat or cold, or good or evil, happens to touch the shadow of a man’s body, it affects not in the least the man himself, who is distinct from the shadow.

505.shloka:
न साक्षिणं साक्ष्यधर्माः संस्पृशन्ति विलक्षणम् ।
अविकारमुदासीनं गृहधर्माः प्रदीपवत् ॥ ५0५ ॥
505.transliteration:
na sākṣiṇaṃ sākṣyadharmāḥ saṃspṛśanti vilakṣaṇam |
avikāramudāsīnaṃ gṛhadharmāḥ pradīpavat || 505 ||
505.translation: The properties of things observed do not affect the Witness, which is distinct from them, changeless and indifferent – as the properties of a room (do not affect) the lamp (that illumines it).

506.shloka:
रवेर्यथा कर्मणि साक्षिभावो वन्हेर्यथा दाहनियामकत्वम् ।
रज्जोर्यथारोपितवस्तुसङ्गः तथैव कूटस्थचिदात्मनो मे ॥ ५0६ ॥
506.transliteration:
raveryathā karmaṇi sākṣibhāvo vanheryathā dāhaniyāmakatvam |
rajjoryathāropitavastusaṅgaḥ tathaiva kūṭasthacidātmano me || 506 ||
506.translation: As the sun is a mere witness of men’s actions, as fire burns everything without distinction, and as the rope is related to a thing superimposed on it, so am I, the unchangeable Self, the Intelligence Absolute.

507.shloka:
कर्तापि वा कारयितापि नाहं भोक्तापि वा भोजयितापि नाहम् ।
द्रष्टापि वा दर्शयितापि नाहं सोऽहं स्वयंज्योतिरनीदृगात्मा ॥ ५0७ ॥
507.transliteration:
kartāpi vā kārayitāpi nāhaṃ bhoktāpi vā bhojayitāpi nāham |
draṣṭāpi vā darśayitāpi nāhaṃ so'haṃ svayaṃjyotiranīdṛgātmā || 507 ||
507.translation: I neither do nor make others do any action; I neither enjoy nor make others enjoy; I neither see nor make others see; I am that Self-effulgent, Transcendent Ātman.

508.shloka:
चलत्युपाधौ प्रतिबिम्बलौल्यम् अउपाधिकं मूढधियो नयन्ति ।
स्वबिम्बभूतं रविवद्विनिष्क्रियं कर्तास्मि भोक्तास्मि हतोऽस्मि हेति ॥ ५0८ ॥
508.transliteration:
calatyupādhau pratibimbalaulyam aupādhikaṃ mūḍhadhiyo nayanti |
svabimbabhūtaṃ ravivadviniṣkriyaṃ kartāsmi bhoktāsmi hato'smi heti || 508 ||
508.translation: When the supervening adjunct (Upādhi) is moving, the resulting movement of the reflection is ascribed by fools to the object reflected, such as the sun, which is free from activity – (and they think) 'I am the doer', 'I am the experiencer', 'I am killed, oh, alas!'

509.shloka:
जले वापि स्थले वापि लुठत्वेष जडात्मकः ।
नाहं विलिप्ये तद्धर्मैर्घटधर्मैर्नभो यथा ॥ ५0९ ॥
509.transliteration:
jale vāpi sthale vāpi luṭhatveṣa jaḍātmakaḥ |
nāhaṃ vilipye taddharmairghaṭadharmairnabho yathā || 509 ||
509.translation: Let this inert body drop down in water or on land. I am not touched by its properties, like the sky by the properties of the jar.

510.shloka:
कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वखलत्वमत्तता जडत्वबद्धत्वविमुक्ततादयः ।
बुद्धेर्विकल्पा न तु सन्ति वस्तुतः स्वस्मिन् परे ब्रह्मणि केवलेऽद्वये ॥ ५१0 ॥
510.transliteration:
kartṛtvabhoktṛtvakhalatvamattatā jaḍatvabaddhatvavimuktatādayaḥ |
buddhervikalpā na tu santi vastutaḥ svasmin pare brahmaṇi kevale'dvaye || 510 ||
510.translation: The passing states of the Buddhi, such as agency, experience, cunning, drunkenness, dullness, bondage and freedom, are never in reality in the Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Absolute, the one without a second.

511.shloka:
सन्तु विकाराः प्रकृतेर्दशधा शतधा सहस्रधा वापि ।
किं मेऽसङ्गचितस्तैर्न घनः क्वचिदम्बरं स्पृशति ॥ ५११ ॥
511.transliteration:
santu vikārāḥ prakṛterdaśadhā śatadhā sahasradhā vāpi |
kiṃ me'saṅgacitastairna ghanaḥ kvacidambaraṃ spṛśati || 511 ||
511.translation: Let there be changes in the Prakriti in ten, a hundred, or a thousand ways, what have I, the unattached Knowledge Absolute, got to do with them? Never do the clouds touch the sky!

512.shloka:
अव्यक्तादिस्थूलपर्यन्तमेतत् विश्व यत्राभासमात्रं प्रतीतम् ।
व्योमप्रख्यं सूक्ष्ममाद्यन्तहीनं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१२ ॥
512.transliteration:
avyaktādisthūlaparyantametat viśva yatrābhāsamātraṃ pratītam |
vyomaprakhyaṃ sūkṣmamādyantahīnaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 512 ||
512.translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is like the sky, subtle, without beginning or end, in which the whole universe from the Undifferentiated down to the gross body, appears merely as a shadow.

513.shloka:
सर्वाधारं सर्ववस्तुप्रकाशं सर्वाकारं सर्वगं सर्वशून्यम् ।
नित्यं शुद्धं निश्चलं निर्विकल्पं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१३ ॥
513.transliteration:
sarvādhāraṃ sarvavastuprakāśaṃ sarvākāraṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaśūnyam |
nityaṃ śuddhaṃ niścalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 513 ||
513.translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is the support of all, which illumines all things, which has infinite forms, is omnipresent, devoid of multiplicity, eternal, pure, unmoved and absolute.

514.shloka:
यत्प्रत्यस्ताशेषमायाविशेषं प्रत्यग्रूपं प्रत्ययागम्यमानम् ।
सत्यज्ञानानन्तमानन्दरूपं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१४ ॥
514.transliteration:
yatpratyastāśeṣamāyāviśeṣaṃ pratyagrūpaṃ pratyayāgamyamānam |
satyajñānānantamānandarūpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 514 ||
514.translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which transcends the endless differentiations of Māyā, which is the inmost essence of all, is beyond the range of consciousness, and which is Truth, Knowledge, Infinity and Bliss Absolute.

515.shloka:
निष्क्रियोऽस्म्यविकारोऽस्मि निष्कलोऽस्मि निराकृतिः ।
निर्विकल्पोऽस्मि नित्योऽस्मि निरालम्बोऽस्मि निर्द्वयः ॥ ५१५ ॥
515.transliteration:
niṣkriyo'smyavikāro'smi niṣkalo'smi nirākṛtiḥ |
nirvikalpo'smi nityo'smi nirālambo'smi nirdvayaḥ || 515 ||
515.translation: I am without activity, changeless, without parts, formless, absolute, eternal, without any other support, the One without a second.

516.translation: I am the Universal, I am the All, I am transcendent, the One without a second. I am Absolute and Infinite Knowledge, I am Bliss and indivisible.

517.shloka:
स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यविभूतिरेषा भवत्कृपाश्रीमहिमप्रसादात् ।
प्राप्ता मया श्रीगुरवे महात्मने नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु पुनर्नमोऽस्तु ॥ ५१७ ॥
517.transliteration:
svārājyasāmrājyavibhūtireṣā bhavatkṛpāśrīmahimaprasādāt |
prāptā mayā śrīgurave mahātmane namo namaste'stu punarnamo'stu || 517 ||
517.translation: This splendour of the sovereignty of Self-effulgence I have received by virtue of the supreme majesty of thy grace. Salutations to thee, O glorious, noble-minded Teacher, salutations again and again!

518.shloka:
महास्वप्ने मायाकृतजनिजरामृत्युगहने भ्रमन्तं क्लिश्यन्तं बहुलतरतापैरनुदिनम् ।
अहंकारव्याघ्रव्यथितमिममत्यन्तकृपया प्रबोध्य प्रस्वापात्परमवितवान्मामसि गुरो ॥ ५१८ ॥
518.transliteration:
mahāsvapne māyākṛtajanijarāmṛtyugahane bhramantaṃ kliśyantaṃ bahulataratāpairanudinam |
ahaṃkāravyāghravyathitamimamatyantakṛpayā prabodhya prasvāpātparamavitavānmāmasi guro || 518 ||
518.translation: O Master, thou hast out of sheer grace awakened me from sleep and completely saved me, who was wandering, in an interminable dream, in a forest of birth, decay and death created by illusion, being tormented day after day by countless afflictions, and sorely troubled by the tiger of egoism.

519.shloka:
नमस्तस्मै सदैकस्मै कस्मैचिन्महसे नमः ।
यदेतद्विश्वरूपेण राजते गुरुराज ते ॥ ५१९ ॥
519.transliteration:
namastasmai sadaikasmai kasmaicinmahase namaḥ |
yadetadviśvarūpeṇa rājate gururāja te || 519 ||
519.translation: Salutations to thee, O Prince of Teachers, thou unnamable Greatness, that art ever the same and dost manifest thyself as this universe – thee I salute.

520.shloka:
इति नतमवलोक्य शिष्यवर्यं समधिगतात्मसुखं प्रबुद्धतत्त्वम् ।
प्रमुदितहृदयं स देशिकेन्द्रः पुनरिदमाह वचः परं महात्मा ॥ ५२0 ॥
520.transliteration:
iti natamavalokya śiṣyavaryaṃ samadhigatātmasukhaṃ prabuddhatattvam |
pramuditahṛdayaṃ sa deśikendraḥ punaridamāha vacaḥ paraṃ mahātmā || 520 ||
520.translation: Seeing the worthy disciple, who had attained the Bliss of the self, realised the Truth and was glad at heart, thus prostrating himself, that noble, ideal Teacher again addressed the following excellent words:

521.shloka:
ब्रह्मप्रत्ययसन्ततिर्जगदतो ब्रह्मैव तत्सर्वतः पश्याध्यात्मदृशा प्रशान्तमनसा सर्वास्ववस्थास्वपि ।
रूपादन्यदवेक्षितं किमभितश्चक्षुष्मतां दृश्यते तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदः सतः किमपरं बुद्धेर्विहारास्पदम् ॥ ५२१ ॥
521.transliteration:
brahmapratyayasantatirjagadato brahmaiva tatsarvataḥ paśyādhyātmadṛśā praśāntamanasā sarvāsvavasthāsvapi |
rūpādanyadavekṣitaṃ kimabhitaścakṣuṣmatāṃ dṛśyate tadvadbrahmavidaḥ sataḥ kimaparaṃ buddhervihārāspadam || 521 ||
521.translation: The universe is an unbroken series of perceptions of Brahman; hence it is in all respects nothing but Brahman. See this with the eye of illumination and a serene mind, under all circumstances. Is one who has eyes ever found to see all around anything else but forms? Similarly, what is there except Brahman to engage the intellect of a man of realisation?

522.shloka:
कस्तां परानन्दरसानुभूति मृत्सृज्य शून्येषु रमेत विद्वान् ।
चन्द्रे महाल्हादिनि दीप्यमाने चित्रेन्दुमालोकयितुं क इच्छेत् ॥ ५२२ ॥
522.transliteration:
kastāṃ parānandarasānubhūti mṛtsṛjya śūnyeṣu rameta vidvān |
candre mahālhādini dīpyamāne citrendumālokayituṃ ka icchet || 522 ||
522.translation: What wise man would discard that enjoyment of Supreme Bliss and revel in things unsubstantial? When the exceedingly charming moon is shining, who would wish to look at a painted moon?

523.shloka:
असत्पदार्थानुभवेन किंचिन् न ह्यस्ति तृप्तिर्न च दुःखहानिः ।
तदद्वयानन्दरसानुभूत्या तृप्तः सुखं तिष्ठ सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥ ५२३ ॥
523.transliteration:
asatpadārthānubhavena kiṃcin na hyasti tṛptirna ca duḥkhahāniḥ |
tadadvayānandarasānubhūtyā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ tiṣṭha sadātmaniṣṭhayā || 523 ||
523.translation: From the perception of unreal things there is neither satisfaction nor a cessation of misery. Therefore, being satisfied with the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, live happily in a state of identity with that Reality.

524.shloka:
स्वमेव सर्वथा पश्यन्मन्यमानः स्वमद्वयम् ।
स्वानन्दमनुभुञ्जानः कालं नय महामते ॥ ५२४ ॥
524.transliteration:
svameva sarvathā paśyanmanyamānaḥ svamadvayam |
svānandamanubhuñjānaḥ kālaṃ naya mahāmate || 524 ||
524.translation: Beholding the Self alone in all circumstances, thinking of the Self, the One without a second, and enjoying the Bliss of the Self, pass thy time, O noble soul!

525.shloka:
अखण्डबोधात्मनि निर्विकल्पे विकल्पनं व्योम्नि पुरप्रकल्पनम् ।
तदद्वयानन्दमयात्मना सदा शान्तिं परामेत्य भजस्व मौनम् ॥ ५२५ ॥
525.transliteration:
akhaṇḍabodhātmani nirvikalpe vikalpanaṃ vyomni puraprakalpanam |
tadadvayānandamayātmanā sadā śāntiṃ parāmetya bhajasva maunam || 525 ||
525.translation: Dualistic conceptions in the Ātman, the Infinite Knowledge, the Absolute, are like imagining castles in the air. Therefore, always identifying thyself with the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thereby attaining Supreme Peace, remain quiet.

526.shloka:
तूष्णीमवस्था परमोपशान्तिः बुद्धेरसत्कल्पविकल्पहेतोः ।
ब्रह्मात्मन ब्रह्मविदो महात्मनो यत्राद्वयानन्दसुखं निरन्तरम् ॥ ५२६ ॥
526.transliteration:
tūṣṇīmavasthā paramopaśāntiḥ buddherasatkalpavikalpahetoḥ |
brahmātmana brahmavido mahātmano yatrādvayānandasukhaṃ nirantaram || 526 ||
526.translation: To the sage who has realised Brahman, the mind, which is the cause of unreal fancies, becomes perfectly tranquil. This verily is his state of quietude, in which, identified with Brahman, he has constant enjoyment of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second.

527.translation: To the man who has realised his own nature, and drinks the undiluted Bliss of the Self, there is nothing more exhilarating than the quietude that comes of a state of desirelessness.

528.shloka:
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्नुपविशञ्छयानो वान्यथापि वा ।
यथेच्छया वेसेद्विद्वानात्नारामः सदा मुनिः ॥ ५२८ ॥
528.transliteration:
gacchaṃstiṣṭhannupaviśañchayāno vānyathāpi vā |
yathecchayā vesedvidvānātnārāmaḥ sadā muniḥ || 528 ||
528.translation: The illumined sage, whose only pleasure is in the Self, ever lives at ease, whether going or staying, sitting or lying, or in any other condition.

529.shloka:
न देशकालासनदिग्यमादि लक्ष्याद्यपेक्षाप्रतिबद्धवृत्तेः ।
संसिद्धतत्त्वस्य महात्मनोऽस्ति स्ववेदने का नियमाद्यवस्था ॥ ५२९ ॥
529.transliteration:
na deśakālāsanadigyamādi lakṣyādyapekṣāpratibaddhavṛtteḥ |
saṃsiddhatattvasya mahātmano'sti svavedane kā niyamādyavasthā || 529 ||
529.translation: The noble soul who has perfectly realised the Truth, and whose mind-functions meet with no obstruction, no more depends upon conditions of place, time, posture, direction, moral disciplines, objects of meditation and so forth. What regulative conditions can there be in knowing one’s own Self?

530.shloka:
घटोऽयमिति विज्ञातुं नियमः कोऽन्ववेक्षते ।
विना प्रमाणसुष्ठुत्वं यस्मिन् सति पदार्थधीः ॥ ५३0 ॥
530.transliteration:
ghaṭo'yamiti vijñātuṃ niyamaḥ ko'nvavekṣate |
vinā pramāṇasuṣṭhutvaṃ yasmin sati padārthadhīḥ || 530 ||
530.translation: To know that this is a jar, what condition, forsooth, is necessary except that the means of knowledge be free from defect, which alone ensures a cognition of the object?

531.shloka:
अयमात्मा नित्यसिद्धः प्रमाणे सति भासते ।
न देशं नापि कालं न शुद्धिं वाप्यपेक्षते ॥ ५३१ ॥
531.transliteration:
ayamātmā nityasiddhaḥ pramāṇe sati bhāsate |
na deśaṃ nāpi kālaṃ na śuddhiṃ vāpyapekṣate || 531 ||
531.translation: So this Ātman, which is an eternal verity, manifests Itself as soon as the right means of knowledge is present, and does not depend upon either place or time or (internal) purity.

532.translation: The consciousness, 'I am Devadatta', is independent of circumstances; similar is the case with the realisation of the knower of Brahman that he is Brahman.

533.shloka:
भानुनेव जगत्सर्वं भासते यस्य तेजसा ।
अनात्मकमसत्तुच्छं किं नु तस्यावभासकम् ॥ ५३३ ॥
533.transliteration:
bhānuneva jagatsarvaṃ bhāsate yasya tejasā |
anātmakamasattucchaṃ kiṃ nu tasyāvabhāsakam || 533 ||
533.translation: What indeed can manifest That whose lustre, like the sun, causes the whole universe – unsubstantial, unreal, insignificant – to appear at all?

534.shloka:
वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि भूतानि सकलान्यपि ।
येनार्थवन्ति तं किन्नु विज्ञातारं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ ५३४ ॥
534.transliteration:
vedaśāstrapurāṇāni bhūtāni sakalānyapi |
yenārthavanti taṃ kinnu vijñātāraṃ prakāśayet || 534 ||
534.translation: What, indeed, can illumine that Eternal Subject by which the Vedas and Puranas and other Scriptures, as well as all beings are endowed with a meaning?

535.shloka:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरनन्तशक्तिः आत्माप्रमेयः सकलानुभूतिः ।
यमेव विज्ञाय विमुक्तबन्धो जयत्ययं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमोत्तमः ॥ ५३५ ॥
535.transliteration:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiranantaśaktiḥ ātmāprameyaḥ sakalānubhūtiḥ |
yameva vijñāya vimuktabandho jayatyayaṃ brahmaviduttamottamaḥ || 535 ||
535.translation: Here is the Self-effulgent Ātman, of infinite power, beyond the range of conditioned knowledge, yet the common experience of all - realising which alone this incomparable knower of Brahman lives his glorious life, freed from bondage.

536.shloka:
न खिद्यते नो विषयैः प्रमोदते न सज्जते नापि विरज्यते च ।
स्वस्मिन्सदा क्रीडति नन्दति स्वयं निरन्तरानन्दरसेन तृप्तः ॥ ५३६ ॥
536.transliteration:
na khidyate no viṣayaiḥ pramodate na sajjate nāpi virajyate ca |
svasminsadā krīḍati nandati svayaṃ nirantarānandarasena tṛptaḥ || 536 ||
536.translation: Satisfied with undiluted, constant Bliss, he is neither grieved nor elated by sense- objects, is neither attached nor averse to them, but always disports with the Self and takes pleasure therein.

537.shloka:
क्षुधां देहव्यथां त्यक्त्वा बालः क्रीडति वस्तुनिः ।
तथैव विद्वान् रमते निर्ममो निरहं सुखी ॥ ५३७ ॥
537.transliteration:
kṣudhāṃ dehavyathāṃ tyaktvā bālaḥ krīḍati vastuniḥ |
tathaiva vidvān ramate nirmamo nirahaṃ sukhī || 537 ||
537.translation: A child plays with its toys forgetting hunger and bodily pains; exactly so does the man of realisation take pleasure in the Reality, without ideas of 'I' or 'mine', and is happy.

538.shloka:
चिन्ताशून्यमदैन्यभैक्षमशनं पानं सरिद्वारिषु स्वातन्त्र्येण निरङ्कुशा स्थितिरभीर्निद्रा श्मशाने वने ।
वस्त्रं क्षालनशोषणादिरहितं दिग्वास्तु शय्या मही संचारो निगमान्तवीथिषु विदां क्रीडा परे ब्रह्मणि ॥ ५३८ ॥
538.transliteration:
cintāśūnyamadainyabhaikṣamaśanaṃ pānaṃ saridvāriṣu svātantryeṇa niraṅkuśā sthitirabhīrnidrā śmaśāne vane |
vastraṃ kṣālanaśoṣaṇādirahitaṃ digvāstu śayyā mahī saṃcāro nigamāntavīthiṣu vidāṃ krīḍā pare brahmaṇi || 538 ||
538.translation: Men of realisation have their food without anxiety or humiliation by begging, and their drink from the water of rivers; they live freely and independently, and sleep without fear in cremation grounds or forests; their clothing may be the quarters themselves, which need no washing and drying, or any bark etc., the earth is their bed; they roam in the avenue of the Vedanta; while their pastime is in the Supreme Brahman.

539.shloka:
विमानमालम्ब्य शरीरमेतद् भुनक्त्यशेषान्विषयानुपस्थितान् ।
परेच्छया बालवदात्मवेत्ता योऽव्यक्तलिङ्गोऽननुषक्तबाह्यः ॥ ५३९ ॥
539.transliteration:
vimānamālambya śarīrametad bhunaktyaśeṣānviṣayānupasthitān |
parecchayā bālavadātmavettā yo'vyaktaliṅgo'nanuṣaktabāhyaḥ || 539 ||
539.translation: The knower of the Ātman, who wears no outward mark and is unattached to external things, rests on this body without identification, and experiences all sorts of sense-objects as they come, through others’ wish, like a child.

540.shloka:
दिगम्बरो वापि च साम्बरो वा त्वगम्बरो वापि चिदम्बरस्थः ।
उन्मत्तवद्वापि च बालवद्वा पिशाचवद्वापि चरत्यवन्याम् ॥ ५४0 ॥
540.transliteration:
digambaro vāpi ca sāmbaro vā tvagambaro vāpi cidambarasthaḥ |
unmattavadvāpi ca bālavadvā piśācavadvāpi caratyavanyām || 540 ||
540.translation: Established in the ethereal plane of Absolute Knowledge, he wanders in the world, sometimes like a madman, sometimes like a child and at other times like a ghoul, having no other clothes on his person except the quarters, or sometimes wearing clothes, or perhaps skins at other times.

541.shloka:
कामान्निष्कामरूपी संश्चरत्येकचारो मुनिः ।
स्वात्मनैव सदा तुष्टः स्वयं सर्वात्मना स्थितः ॥ ५४१ ॥
541.transliteration:
kāmānniṣkāmarūpī saṃścaratyekacāro muniḥ |
svātmanaiva sadā tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sarvātmanā sthitaḥ || 541 ||
541.translation: The sage, living alone, enjoys the sense-objects, being the very embodiment of desirelessness – always satisfied with his own Self, and himself present at the All.

542.shloka:
क्वचिन्मूढो विद्वान् क्वचिदपि महाराजविभवः क्वचिद्भ्रान्तः सौम्यः क्वचिदजगराचारकलितः ।
क्वचित्पात्रीभूतः क्वचिदवमतः क्वाप्यविदितः चरत्येवं प्राज्ञः सततपरमानन्दसुखितः ॥ ५४२ ॥
542.transliteration:
kvacinmūḍho vidvān kvacidapi mahārājavibhavaḥ kvacidbhrāntaḥ saumyaḥ kvacidajagarācārakalitaḥ |
kvacitpātrībhūtaḥ kvacidavamataḥ kvāpyaviditaḥ caratyevaṃ prājñaḥ satataparamānandasukhitaḥ || 542 ||
542.translation: Sometimes a fool, sometimes a sage, sometimes possessed of regal splendour; sometimes wandering, sometimes behaving like a motionless python, sometimes wearing a benignant expression; sometimes honoured, sometimes insulted, sometimes unknown – thus lives the man of realisation, ever happy with Supreme Bliss.

543.shloka:
निर्धनोऽपि सदा तुष्टोऽप्यसहायो महाबलः ।
नित्यतृप्तोऽप्यभुञ्जानोऽप्यसमः समदर्शनः ॥ ५४३ ॥
543.transliteration:
nirdhano'pi sadā tuṣṭo'pyasahāyo mahābalaḥ |
nityatṛpto'pyabhuñjāno'pyasamaḥ samadarśanaḥ || 543 ||
543.translation: Though without riches, yet ever content; though helpless, yet very powerful, though not enjoying the sense-objects, yet eternally satisfied; though without an exemplar, yet looking upon all with an eye of equality.

544.shloka:
अपि कुर्वन्नकुर्वाणश्चाभोक्ता फलभोग्यपि ।
शरीर्यप्यशरीर्येष परिच्छिन्नोऽपि सर्वगः ॥ ५४४ ॥
544.transliteration:
api kurvannakurvāṇaścābhoktā phalabhogyapi |
śarīryapyaśarīryeṣa paricchinno'pi sarvagaḥ || 544 ||
544.translation: Though doing, yet inactive; though experiencing fruits of past actions, yet untouched by them; though possessed of a body, yet without identification with it; though limited, yet omnipresent is he.

545.shloka:
अशरीरं सदा सन्तमिमं ब्रह्मविदं क्वचित् ।
प्रियाप्रिये न स्पृशतस्तथैव च शुभाशुभे ॥ ५४५ ॥
545.transliteration:
aśarīraṃ sadā santamimaṃ brahmavidaṃ kvacit |
priyāpriye na spṛśatastathaiva ca śubhāśubhe || 545 ||
545.translation: Neither pleasure nor pain, nor good nor evil, ever touches this knower of Brahman, who always lives without the body-idea.

546.shloka:
स्थूलादिसंबन्धवतोऽभिमानिनः सुखं च दुःखं च शुभाशुभे च ।
विध्वस्तबन्धस्य सदात्मनो मुनेः कुतः शुभं वाप्यशुभं फलं वा ॥ ५४६ ॥
546.transliteration:
sthūlādisaṃbandhavato'bhimāninaḥ sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca śubhāśubhe ca |
vidhvastabandhasya sadātmano muneḥ kutaḥ śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ phalaṃ vā || 546 ||
546.translation: Pleasure or pain, or good or evil, affects only him who has connections with the gross body etc., and identifies himself with these. How can good or evil, or their effects, touch the sage who has identified himself with the Reality and thereby shattered his bondage?

547.shloka:
तमसा ग्रस्तवद्भानादग्रस्तोऽपि रविर्जनैः ।
ग्रस्त इत्युच्यते भ्रान्त्यां ह्यज्ञात्वा वस्तुलक्षणम् ॥ ५४७ ॥
547.transliteration:
tamasā grastavadbhānādagrasto'pi ravirjanaiḥ |
grasta ityucyate bhrāntyāṃ hyajñātvā vastulakṣaṇam || 547 ||
547.translation: The sun which appears to be, but is not actually, swallowed by Rāhu, is said to be swallowed, on account of delusion, by people, not knowing the real nature of the sun.

548.shloka:
तद्वद्देहादिबन्धेभ्यो विमुक्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम् ।
पश्यन्ति देहिवन्मूढाः शरीराभासदर्शनात् ॥ ५४८ ॥
548.transliteration:
tadvaddehādibandhebhyo vimuktaṃ brahmavittamam |
paśyanti dehivanmūḍhāḥ śarīrābhāsadarśanāt || 548 ||
548.translation: Similarly, ignorant people look upon the perfect knower of Brahman, who is wholly rid of bondages of the body etc., as possessed of the body, seeing but an appearance of it.

549.shloka:
अहिर्निर्ल्वयनीं वायं मुक्त्वा देहं तु तिष्ठति ।
इतस्ततश्चाल्यमानो यत्किंचित्प्राणवायुना ॥ ५४९ ॥
549.transliteration:
ahirnirlvayanīṃ vāyaṃ muktvā dehaṃ tu tiṣṭhati |
itastataścālyamāno yatkiṃcitprāṇavāyunā || 549 ||
549.translation: In reality, however, he rests discarding the body, like the snake its slough; and the body is moved hither and thither by the force of the Prāṇa, just as it listeth.

550.shloka:
स्त्रोतसा नीयते दारु यथा निम्नोन्नतस्थलम् ।
दैवेन नीयते देहो यथाकालोपभुक्तिषु ॥ ५५0 ॥
550.transliteration:
strotasā nīyate dāru yathā nimnonnatasthalam |
daivena nīyate deho yathākālopabhuktiṣu || 550 ||
550.translation: As a piece of wood is drifted on to a high or low ground by the current, so is his body carried on by the momentum of past actions to the varied experience of their fruits, as these present themselves in due course.

551.shloka:
प्रारब्धकर्मपरिकल्पितवासनाभिः संसारिवच्चरति भुक्तिषु मुक्तदेहः ।
सिद्धः स्वयं वसति साक्षिवदत्र तूष्णीं चक्रस्य मूलमिव कल्पविकल्पशून्यः ॥ ५५१ ॥
551.transliteration:
prārabdhakarmaparikalpitavāsanābhiḥ saṃsārivaccarati bhuktiṣu muktadehaḥ |
siddhaḥ svayaṃ vasati sākṣivadatra tūṣṇīṃ cakrasya mūlamiva kalpavikalpaśūnyaḥ || 551 ||
551.translation: The man of realisation, bereft of the body-idea, moves amid sense-enjoyments like a man subject to transmigration, through desires engendered by Prārabdha work. He himself, however, lives unmoved in the body, like a witness, free from mental oscillations, like the pivot of the potter’s wheel.

552.shloka:
नैवेन्द्रियाणि विषयेषु नियुङ्क्त एष नैवापयुङ्क्त उप्दर्शनलक्षणस्थः ।
नैव क्रियाफलमपीषदवेक्षते स स्वानन्दसान्द्ररसपानसुमत्तचित्तः ॥ ५५२ ॥
552.transliteration:
naivendriyāṇi viṣayeṣu niyuṅkta eṣa naivāpayuṅkta updarśanalakṣaṇasthaḥ |
naiva kriyāphalamapīṣadavekṣate sa svānandasāndrarasapānasumattacittaḥ || 552 ||
552.translation: He neither directs the sense-organs to their objects nor detaches them from these, but stays like an unconcerned spectator. And he has not the least regard for the fruits of actions, his mind being thoroughly inebriated with drinking the undiluted elixir of the Bliss of Ātman.

553.shloka:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्यगतिं त्यक्त्वा यस्तिष्ठेत्केवलात्मना ।
शिव एव स्वयं साक्षादयं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमः ॥ ५५३ ॥
553.transliteration:
lakṣyālakṣyagatiṃ tyaktvā yastiṣṭhetkevalātmanā |
śiva eva svayaṃ sākṣādayaṃ brahmaviduttamaḥ || 553 ||
553.translation: He who, giving up all such considerations as - this is a fit object of meditation and this is not – lives as the absolute Ātman, is verily Śiva himself, and he is the best among Knowers of Brahman.

554.shloka:
जीवन्नेव सदा मुक्तः कृतार्थो ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
उपाधिनाशाद्ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येति निर्द्वयम् ॥ ५५४ ॥
554.transliteration:
jīvanneva sadā muktaḥ kṛtārtho brahmavittamaḥ |
upādhināśādbrahmaiva san brahmāpyeti nirdvayam || 554 ||
554.translation: Through the destruction of the supervening adjuncts, the perfect knower of Brahman merges himself in the One Brahman without a second – which he had been all along – becomes very free even while living, and attains the consummation of his life.

555.shloka:
शैलूषो वेषसद्भावा भावयोश्च यथा पुमान् ।
तथैव ब्रह्मविच्छ्रेष्ठः सदा ब्रह्मैव नापरः ॥ ५५५ ॥
555.transliteration:
śailūṣo veṣasadbhāvā bhāvayośca yathā pumān |
tathaiva brahmavicchreṣṭhaḥ sadā brahmaiva nāparaḥ || 555 ||
555.translation: As an actor, when he puts on the dress of his role, or when he does not, is always a man, so the perfect knower of Brahman is always Brahman and nothing else.

556.shloka:
यत्र क्वापि विशीर्णं सत्पर्णमिव तरोर्वपुः पततात् ।
ब्रह्मीभूतस्य यतेः प्रागेव तच्चिदग्निना दग्धम् ॥ ५५६ ॥
556.transliteration:
yatra kvāpi viśīrṇaṃ satparṇamiva tarorvapuḥ patatāt |
brahmībhūtasya yateḥ prāgeva taccidagninā dagdham || 556 ||
556.translation: Let the body of the Sannyasin who has realised his identity with Brahman, wither and fall anywhere like the leaf of a tree, (it is of little consequence to him, for) it has already been burnt by the fire of knowledge.

557.shloka:
सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि तिष्ठतो मुनेः पूर्णाद्वयानन्दमयात्मना सदा ।
न देशकालाद्युचितप्रतीक्षा त्वङ्मांसविट्पिण्डविसर्जनाय ॥ ५५७ ॥
557.transliteration:
sadātmani brahmaṇi tiṣṭhato muneḥ pūrṇādvayānandamayātmanā sadā |
na deśakālādyucitapratīkṣā tvaṅmāṃsaviṭpiṇḍavisarjanāya || 557 ||
557.translation: The sage who always lives in the Reality – Brahman – as Infinite Bliss, the One without a second, does not depend upon the customary considerations of place, time, etc., for giving up this mass of skin, flesh and filth.

558.shloka:
देहस्य मोक्षो नो मोक्षो न दण्डस्य कमण्डलोः ।
अविद्याहृदयग्रन्थिमोक्षो मोक्षो यतस्ततः ॥ ५५८ ॥
558.transliteration:
dehasya mokṣo no mokṣo na daṇḍasya kamaṇḍaloḥ |
avidyāhṛdayagranthimokṣo mokṣo yatastataḥ || 558 ||
558.translation: For the giving up of the body is not Liberation, nor that of the staff and the water- bowl; but Liberation consists in the destruction of the heart’s knot which is Nescience.

559.shloka:
कुल्यायामथ नद्यां वा शिवक्षेत्रेऽपि चत्वरे ।
पर्णं पतति चेत्तेन तरोः किं नु शुभाशुभम् ॥ ५५९ ॥
559.transliteration:
kulyāyāmatha nadyāṃ vā śivakṣetre'pi catvare |
parṇaṃ patati cettena taroḥ kiṃ nu śubhāśubham || 559 ||
559.translation: If a leaf falls in a small stream, or a river, or a place consecrated by Shiva, or in a crossing of roads, of what good or evil effect is that to the tree?

560.shloka:
पत्रस्य पुष्पस्य फलस्य नाशवद् देहेन्द्रियप्राणधियां विनाशः ।
नैवात्मनः स्वस्य सदात्मकस्या नन्दाकृतेर्वृक्षवदस्ति चैषः ॥ ५६0 ॥
560.transliteration:
patrasya puṣpasya phalasya nāśavad dehendriyaprāṇadhiyāṃ vināśaḥ |
naivātmanaḥ svasya sadātmakasyā nandākṛtervṛkṣavadasti caiṣaḥ || 560 ||
560.translation: The destruction of the body, organs, Prāṇas and Buddhi is like that of a leaf or flower or fruit (to a tree). It does not affect the Ātman, the Reality, the Embodiment of Bliss – which is one’s true nature. That survives, like the tree.

561.shloka:
प्रज्ञानघन इत्यात्मलक्षणं सत्यसूचकम् ।
अनूद्यौपाधिकस्यैव कथयन्ति विनाशनम् ॥ ५६१ ॥
561.transliteration:
prajñānaghana ityātmalakṣaṇaṃ satyasūcakam |
anūdyaupādhikasyaiva kathayanti vināśanam || 561 ||
561.translation: The Śrutis, by setting forth the real nature of the Ātman in the words, "The Embodiment of Knowledge" etc., which indicate Its Reality, speak of the destruction of the apparent limitations merely.

562.shloka:
अविनाशी वा अरेऽयमात्मेति श्रुतिरात्मनः ।
प्रब्रवीत्यविनाशित्वं विनश्यत्सु विकारिषु ॥ ५६२ ॥
562.transliteration:
avināśī vā are'yamātmeti śrutirātmanaḥ |
prabravītyavināśitvaṃ vinaśyatsu vikāriṣu || 562 ||
562.translation: The Śruti passage, "Verily is this Ātman immortal, my dear", mentions the immortality of the Ātman in the midst of things perishable and subject to modification.

563.shloka:
पाषाणवृक्षतृणधान्यकडङ्कराद्या दग्धा भवन्ति हि मृदेव यथा तथैव ।
देहेन्द्रियासुमन आदि समस्तदृश्यं ज्ञानाग्निदग्धमुपयाति परात्मभावम् ॥ ५६३ ॥
563.transliteration:
pāṣāṇavṛkṣatṛṇadhānyakaḍaṅkarādyā dagdhā bhavanti hi mṛdeva yathā tathaiva |
dehendriyāsumana ādi samastadṛśyaṃ jñānāgnidagdhamupayāti parātmabhāvam || 563 ||
563.translation: Just as a stone, a tree, grass, paddy, husk, etc., when burnt, are reduced to earth (ashes) only, even so the whole objective universe comprising the body, organs, Prāṇas, Manas and so forth, are, when burnt by the fire of realisation, reduced to the Supreme Self.

564.shloka:
विलक्षणं यथा ध्वान्तं लीयते भानुतेजसि ।
तथैव सकलं दृश्यं ब्रह्मणि प्रविलीयते ॥ ५६४ ॥
564.transliteration:
vilakṣaṇaṃ yathā dhvāntaṃ līyate bhānutejasi |
tathaiva sakalaṃ dṛśyaṃ brahmaṇi pravilīyate || 564 ||
564.translation: As darkness, which is distinct (from sunshine), vanishes in the sun’s radiance, so the whole objective universe dissolves in Brahman.

565.shloka:
घटे नष्टे यथा व्योम व्योमैव भवति स्फुटम् ।
तथैवोपाधिविलये ब्रह्मैव ब्रह्मवित्स्वयम् ॥ ५६५ ॥
565.transliteration:
ghaṭe naṣṭe yathā vyoma vyomaiva bhavati sphuṭam |
tathaivopādhivilaye brahmaiva brahmavitsvayam || 565 ||
565.translation: As, when a jar is broken, the space enclosed by it becomes palpably the limitless space, so when the apparent limitations are destroyed, the knower of Brahman verily becomes Brahman Itself.

566.shloka:
क्षीरं क्षीरे यथा क्षिप्तं तैलं तैले जलं जले ।
संयुक्तमेकतां याति तथात्मन्यात्मविन्मुनिः ॥ ५६६ ॥
566.transliteration:
kṣīraṃ kṣīre yathā kṣiptaṃ tailaṃ taile jalaṃ jale |
saṃyuktamekatāṃ yāti tathātmanyātmavinmuniḥ || 566 ||
566.translation: As milk poured into milk, oil into oil, and water into water, becomes united and one with it, so the sage who has realised the Ātman becomes one in the Ātman.

567.shloka:
एवं विदेहकैवल्यं सन्मात्रत्वमखण्डितम् ।
ब्रह्मभावं प्रपद्यैष यतिर्नावर्तते पुनः ॥ ५६७ ॥
567.transliteration:
evaṃ videhakaivalyaṃ sanmātratvamakhaṇḍitam |
brahmabhāvaṃ prapadyaiṣa yatirnāvartate punaḥ || 567 ||
567.translation: Realising thus the extreme isolation that comes of disembodiedness, and becoming eternally identified with the Absolute Reality, Brahman, the sage no longer suffers transmigration.

568.translation: For his bodies, consisting of Nescience etc., having been burnt by the realisation of the identity of the Jīva and Brahman, he becomes Brahman Itself; and how can Brahman ever have rebirth?

569.shloka:
मायाकॢप्तौ बन्धमोक्षौ न स्तः स्वात्मनि वस्तुतः ।
यथा रज्जौ निष्क्रियायां सर्पाभासविनिर्गमौ ॥ ५६९ ॥
569.transliteration:
māyākḷptau bandhamokṣau na staḥ svātmani vastutaḥ |
yathā rajjau niṣkriyāyāṃ sarpābhāsavinirgamau || 569 ||
569.translation: Bondage and Liberation, which are conjured up by Māyā, do not really exist in the Ātman, one’s Reality, as the appearance and exit of the snake do not abide in the rope, which suffers no change.

570.shloka:
आवृतेः सदसत्त्वाभ्यां वक्तव्ये बन्धमोक्षणे ।
नावृतिर्ब्रह्मणः काचिदन्याभावादनावृतम् यद्यस्त्यद्वैतहानिः स्याद्द्वैतं नो सहते श्रुतिः ॥ ५७0 ॥
570.transliteration:
āvṛteḥ sadasattvābhyāṃ vaktavye bandhamokṣaṇe |
nāvṛtirbrahmaṇaḥ kācidanyābhāvādanāvṛtam yadyastyadvaitahāniḥ syāddvaitaṃ no sahate śrutiḥ || 570 ||
570.translation: Bondage and Liberation may be talked of when there is the presence or absence of a covering veil. But there can be no covering veil for Brahman, which is always uncovered for want of a second thing besides Itself. If there be, the non-duality of Brahman will be contradicted, and the Śrutis can never brook duality.

571.shloka:
बन्धञ्च मोक्षञ्च मृषैव मूढा बुद्धेर्गुणं वस्तुनि कल्पयन्ति ।
दृगावृतिं मेघकृतां यथा रवौ यतोऽद्वयासङ्गचिदेतदक्षरम् ॥ ५७१ ॥
571.transliteration:
bandhañca mokṣañca mṛṣaiva mūḍhā buddherguṇaṃ vastuni kalpayanti |
dṛgāvṛtiṃ meghakṛtāṃ yathā ravau yato'dvayāsaṅgacidetadakṣaram || 571 ||
571.translation: Bondage and Liberation are attributes of the Buddhi which ignorant people falsely superimpose on the Reality, as the covering of the eyes by a cloud is transferred to the sun. For this Immutable Brahman is Knowledge Absolute, the One without a second and unattached.

572.shloka:
अस्तीति प्रत्ययो यश्च यश्च नास्तीति वस्तुनि ।
बुद्धेरेव गुणावेतौ न तु नित्यस्य वस्तुनः ॥ ५७२ ॥
572.transliteration:
astīti pratyayo yaśca yaśca nāstīti vastuni |
buddhereva guṇāvetau na tu nityasya vastunaḥ || 572 ||
572.translation: The idea that bondage exists, and the idea that it does not, are, with reference to the Reality, both attributes of the Buddhi merely, and never belong to the Eternal Reality, Brahman.

573.shloka:
अतस्तौ मायया कॢप्तौ बन्धमोक्षौ न चात्मनि ।
निष्कले निष्क्रिये शान्ते निरवद्ये निरञ्जने अद्वितीये परे तत्त्वे व्योमवत्कल्पना कुतः ॥ ५७३ ॥
573.transliteration:
atastau māyayā kḷptau bandhamokṣau na cātmani |
niṣkale niṣkriye śānte niravadye nirañjane advitīye pare tattve vyomavatkalpanā kutaḥ || 573 ||
573.translation: Hence this bondage and Liberation are created by Māyā, and are not in the Ātman. How can there be any idea of limitation with regard to the Supreme Truth, which is without parts, without activity, calm, unimpeachable, taintless, and One without a second, as there can be none with regard to the infinite sky?

574.shloka:
न निरोधो न चोत्पत्तिर्न बद्धो न च साधकः ।
न मुमुक्षुर्न वै मुक्त इत्येषा परमार्थता ॥ ५७४ ॥
574.transliteration:
na nirodho na cotpattirna baddho na ca sādhakaḥ |
na mumukṣurna vai mukta ityeṣā paramārthatā || 574 ||
574.translation: There is neither death nor birth, neither a bound nor a struggling soul, neither a seeker after Liberation nor a liberated one – this is the ultimate truth.

575.shloka:
सकलनिगमचूडास्वान्तसिद्धान्तरूपं परमिदमतिगुह्यं दर्शितं ते मयाद्य ।
अपगतकलिदोषं कामनिर्मुक्तबुद्धिं स्वसुतवदसकृत्त्वां भाव्यित्वा मुमुक्षुम् ॥ ५७५ ॥
575.transliteration:
sakalanigamacūḍāsvāntasiddhāntarūpaṃ paramidamatiguhyaṃ darśitaṃ te mayādya |
apagatakalidoṣaṃ kāmanirmuktabuddhiṃ svasutavadasakṛttvāṃ bhāvyitvā mumukṣum || 575 ||
575.translation: I have today repeatedly revealed to thee, as to one’s own son, this excellent and profound secret, which is the inmost purport of all Vedanta, the crest of the Vedas – considering thee an aspirant after Liberation, purged of the taints of this Dark Age, and of a mind free from desires.

576.shloka:
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं प्रश्रयेण कृतानतिः ।
स तेन समनुज्ञातो ययौ निर्मुक्तबन्धनः ॥ ५७६ ॥
576.transliteration:
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ praśrayeṇa kṛtānatiḥ |
sa tena samanujñāto yayau nirmuktabandhanaḥ || 576 ||
576.translation: Hearing these words of the Guru, the disciple out of reverence prostrated himself before him, and with his permission went his way, freed from bondage.

577.shloka:
गुरुरेव सदानन्दसिन्धौ निर्मग्नमानसः ।
पावयन्वसुधां सर्वाण्विचचार निरन्तरः ॥ ५७७ ॥
577.transliteration:
gurureva sadānandasindhau nirmagnamānasaḥ |
pāvayanvasudhāṃ sarvāṇvicacāra nirantaraḥ || 577 ||
577.translation: And the Guru, with his mind steeped in the ocean of Existence and Bliss Absolute, roamed, verily purifying the whole world – all differentiating ideas banished from his mind.

578.shloka:
इत्याचार्यस्य शिष्यस्य संवादेनात्मलक्षणम् ।
निरूपितं मुमुक्षूणां सुखबोधोपपत्तये ॥ ५७८ ॥
578.transliteration:
ityācāryasya śiṣyasya saṃvādenātmalakṣaṇam |
nirūpitaṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ sukhabodhopapattaye || 578 ||
578.translation: Thus by way of a dialogue between the Teacher and the disciple, has the nature of the Ātman been ascertained for the easy comprehension of seekers after Liberation.

579.shloka:
हितमिदमुपदेशमाद्रियन्तां विहितनिरस्तसमस्तचित्तदोषाः ।
भवसुखविरताः प्रशान्तचित्ताः श्रुतिरसिका यतयो मुमुक्षवो ये ॥ ५७९ ॥
579.transliteration:
hitamidamupadeśamādriyantāṃ vihitanirastasamastacittadoṣāḥ |
bhavasukhaviratāḥ praśāntacittāḥ śrutirasikā yatayo mumukṣavo ye || 579 ||
579.translation: May those Sannyasins who are seekers after Liberation, who have purged themselves of all taints of the mind by the observance of the prescribed methods, who are averse to worldly pleasures, and who are of serene minds, and take a delight in the Śruti – appreciate this salutary teaching!

580.shloka:
संसाराध्वनि तापभानुकिरणप्रोद्भूतदाहव्यथा खिन्नानां जलकाङ्क्षया मरुभुवि भ्रान्त्या परिभ्राम्यताम् ।
अत्यासन्नसुधाम्बुधिं सुखकरं ब्रह्माद्वयं दर्शयत्य् एषा शंकरभारती विजयते निर्वाणसंदायिनी ॥ ५८0 ॥
580.transliteration:
saṃsārādhvani tāpabhānukiraṇaprodbhūtadāhavyathā khinnānāṃ jalakāṅkṣayā marubhuvi bhrāntyā paribhrāmyatām |
atyāsannasudhāmbudhiṃ sukhakaraṃ brahmādvayaṃ darśayaty eṣā śaṃkarabhāratī vijayate nirvāṇasaṃdāyinī || 580 ||
580.translation: For those who are afflicted, in the way of the world, by the burning pain due to the (scorching) sunshine of threefold misery, and who through delusion wander about in a desert in search of water – for them here is the triumphant message of Shankara pointing out, within easy reach, the soothing ocean of nectar, Brahman, the One without a second – to lead them on to Liberation.
